units.leftText: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.
units.rightText: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and turned away from evil.

units.leftText: He had seven sons and three daughters,
units.rightText: And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters.

units.leftText: and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and a very large number of servants. Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East.
units.rightText: His substance also was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she-asses, and a very great household; so that this man was the greatest of all the children of the east.

units.leftText: Job’s sons would take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
units.rightText: And his sons went and held a feast in the house of each one upon his day; and they sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.

units.leftText: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice. Satan’s First Attack
units.rightText: And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and renounced God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

units.leftText: One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan also came among them.
leftNotes: 1:6 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary; here and throughout Job 1

units.leftText: “Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan. “From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil.

units.leftText: Satan answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
units.rightText: Then Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Doth Job fear God for nought?

units.leftText: Have You not placed a hedge on every side around him and his household and all that he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
units.rightText: Hast not thou made a hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath, on every side? thou hast blessed the work of his hands, and his substance is increased in the land.

units.leftText: But stretch out Your hand and strike all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
units.rightText: But put forth thy hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will renounce thee to thy face.

units.leftText: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “Everything he has is in your hands, but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.” Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD. Job Loses His Children and Possessions
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thy hand. So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah.

units.leftText: One day, while Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
units.rightText: And it fell on a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house,

units.leftText: a messenger came and reported to Job: “While the oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,
units.rightText: that there came a messenger unto Job, and said, The oxen were plowing, and the asses feeding beside them;

units.leftText: the Sabeans swooped down and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
units.rightText: and the Sabeans fell upon them, and took them away: yea, they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

units.leftText: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The fire of God fell from heaven. It burned and consumed the sheep and the servants, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

units.leftText: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels, and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have taken them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

units.leftText: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house;

units.leftText: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on the young people and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
units.rightText: and, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee.

units.leftText: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped,
units.rightText: Then Job arose, and rent his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped;

units.leftText: saying: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
units.rightText: and he said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Jehovah gave, and Jehovah hath taken away; blessed be the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
units.rightText: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.

units.leftText: On another day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them to present himself before Him.
units.rightText: Again it came to pass on the day when the sons of God came to present themselves before Jehovah, that Satan came also among them to present himself before Jehovah.
leftNotes: 2:1 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary; here and throughout Job 2

units.leftText: “Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan. “From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still retains his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job? for there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and turneth away from evil: and he still holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

units.leftText: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give up all he owns in exchange for his life.
units.rightText: And Satan answered Jehovah, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

units.leftText: But stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
units.rightText: But put forth thy hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will renounce thee to thy face.

units.leftText: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “He is in your hands, but you must spare his life.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thy hand; only spare his life.

units.leftText: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
units.rightText: So Satan went forth from the presence of Jehovah, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

units.leftText: And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.
units.rightText: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself therewith; and he sat among the ashes.

units.leftText: Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
units.rightText: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity? renounce God, and die.

units.leftText: “You speak as a foolish woman speaks,” he told her. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?” In all this, Job did not sin in what he said. Job’s Three Friends
units.rightText: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

units.leftText: Now when Job’s three friends— Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite— heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
units.rightText: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to bemoan him and to comfort him.

units.leftText: When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
units.rightText: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his robe, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

units.leftText: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him because they saw how intense his suffering was.
units.rightText: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

units.leftText: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
units.rightText: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

units.leftText: And this is what he said:
units.rightText: And Job answered and said:

units.leftText: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’
units.rightText: Let the day perish wherein I was born, And the night which said, There is a man-child conceived.

units.leftText: If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.
units.rightText: Let that day be darkness; Let not God from above seek for it, Neither let the light shine upon it.

units.leftText: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
units.rightText: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own; Let a cloud dwell upon it; Let all that maketh black the day terrify it.

units.leftText: If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.
units.rightText: As for that night, let thick darkness seize upon it: Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months.

units.leftText: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
units.rightText: Lo, let that night be barren; Let no joyful voice come therein.

units.leftText: May it be cursed by those who curse the day — those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
units.rightText: Let them curse it that curse the day, Who are ready to rouse up leviathan.

units.leftText: May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.
units.rightText: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark: Let it look for light, but have none; Neither let it behold the eyelids of the morning:

units.leftText: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
units.rightText: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes.

units.leftText: Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?
units.rightText: Why died I not from the womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when my mother bare me?

units.leftText: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?
units.rightText: Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breasts, that I should suck?

units.leftText: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
units.rightText: For now should I have lain down and been quiet; I should have slept; then had I been at rest,

units.leftText: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins,
units.rightText: With kings and counsellors of the earth, Who built up waste places for themselves;

units.leftText: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
units.rightText: Or with princes that had gold, Who filled their houses with silver:

units.leftText: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
units.rightText: Or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, As infants that never saw light.

units.leftText: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
units.rightText: There the wicked cease from troubling; And there the weary are at rest.

units.leftText: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
units.rightText: There the prisoners are at ease together; They hear not the voice of the taskmaster.

units.leftText: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
units.rightText: The small and the great are there: And the servant is free from his master.

units.leftText: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,
units.rightText: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, And life unto the bitter in soul;

units.leftText: who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,
units.rightText: Who long for death, but it cometh not, And dig for it more than for hid treasures;

units.leftText: who rejoice and greatly exult when they reach the grave?
units.rightText: Who rejoice exceedingly, And are glad, when they can find the grave?

units.leftText: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
units.rightText: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, And whom God hath hedged in?

units.leftText: I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.
units.rightText: For my sighing cometh before I eat, And my groanings are poured out like water.

units.leftText: For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
units.rightText: For the thing which I fear cometh upon me, And that which I am afraid of cometh unto me.

units.leftText: I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”
units.rightText: I am not at ease, neither am I quiet, neither have I rest; But trouble cometh.

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

units.leftText: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?
units.rightText: If one assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

units.leftText: Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
units.rightText: Behold, thou hast instructed many, And thou hast strengthened the weak hands.

units.leftText: Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.
units.rightText: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, And thou hast made firm the feeble knees.

units.leftText: But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.
units.rightText: But now it is come unto thee, and thou faintest; It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.

units.leftText: Is your reverence not your confidence, and the uprightness of your ways your hope?
units.rightText: Is not thy fear of God thy confidence, And the integrity of thy ways thy hope?

units.leftText: Consider now, I plead: Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
units.rightText: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

units.leftText: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.
units.rightText: According as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, And sow trouble, reap the same.

units.leftText: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
units.rightText: By the breath of God they perish, And by the blast of his anger are they consumed.

units.leftText: The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
units.rightText: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

units.leftText: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
units.rightText: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad.

units.leftText: Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.
units.rightText: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, And mine ear received a whisper thereof.

units.leftText: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
units.rightText: In thoughts from the visions of the night, When deep sleep falleth on men,

units.leftText: fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.
units.rightText: Fear came upon me, and trembling, Which made all my bones to shake.

units.leftText: Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.
units.rightText: Then a spirit passed before my face; The hair of my flesh stood up.

units.leftText: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice:
units.rightText: It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof; A form was before mine eyes: There was silence, and I heard a voice, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
units.rightText: Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

units.leftText: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,
units.rightText: Behold, he putteth no trust in his servants; And his angels he chargeth with folly:

units.leftText: how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who can be crushed like a moth!
units.rightText: How much more them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before the moth!

units.leftText: They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.
units.rightText: Betwixt morning and evening they are destroyed: They perish for ever without any regarding it.

units.leftText: Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’[’’]
units.rightText: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.

units.leftText: “Call out if you please, but who will answer? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
units.rightText: Call now; is there any that will answer thee? And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn?

units.leftText: For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
units.rightText: For vexation killeth the foolish man, And jealousy slayeth the silly one.

units.leftText: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
units.rightText: I have seen the foolish taking root: But suddenly I cursed his habitation.

units.leftText: His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
units.rightText: His children are far from safety, And they are crushed in the gate, Neither is there any to deliver them:

units.leftText: The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
units.rightText: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, And taketh it even out of the thorns; And the snare gapeth for their substance.
leftNotes: 5:5 Or and a snare snatches his wealth

units.leftText: For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.
units.rightText: For affliction cometh not forth from the dust, Neither doth trouble spring out of the ground;

units.leftText: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
units.rightText: But man is born unto trouble, As the sparks fly upward.

units.leftText: However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him—
units.rightText: But as for me, I would seek unto God, And unto God would I commit my cause;

units.leftText: the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.
units.rightText: Who doeth great things and unsearchable, Marvellous things without number:

units.leftText: He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.
units.rightText: Who giveth rain upon the earth, And sendeth waters upon the fields;

units.leftText: He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
units.rightText: So that he setteth up on high those that are low, And those that mourn are exalted to safety.

units.leftText: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.
units.rightText: He frustrateth the devices of the crafty, So that their hands cannot perform their enterprise.

units.leftText: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.
units.rightText: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness; And the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

units.leftText: They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.
units.rightText: They meet with darkness in the day-time, And grope at noonday as in the night.

units.leftText: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.
units.rightText: But he saveth from the sword of their mouth, Even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

units.leftText: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
units.rightText: So the poor hath hope, And iniquity stoppeth her mouth.

units.leftText: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
units.rightText: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: Therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.
leftNotes: 5:17 Hebrew Shaddai; here and throughout Job

units.leftText: For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.
units.rightText: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up; He woundeth, and his hands make whole.

units.leftText: He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
units.rightText: He will deliver thee in six troubles; Yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.

units.leftText: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
units.rightText: In famine he will redeem thee from death; And in war from the power of the sword.

units.leftText: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.
units.rightText: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue; Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh.

units.leftText: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.
units.rightText: At destruction and dearth thou shalt laugh; Neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

units.leftText: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
units.rightText: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field; And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.

units.leftText: You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
units.rightText: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace; And thou shalt visit thy fold, and shalt miss nothing.

units.leftText: You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
units.rightText: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great, And thine offspring as the grass of the earth.

units.leftText: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.
units.rightText: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, Like as a shock of grain cometh in in its season.

units.leftText: Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”
units.rightText: Lo this, we have searched it, so it is; Hear it, and know thou it for thy good.

units.leftText: Then Job replied:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “If only my grief could be weighed and placed with my calamity on the scales.
units.rightText: Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And all my calamity laid in the balances!

units.leftText: For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas — no wonder my words have been rash.
units.rightText: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas: Therefore have my words been rash.

units.leftText: For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
units.rightText: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up: The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

units.leftText: Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
units.rightText: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?

units.leftText: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg ?
units.rightText: Can that which hath no savor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
leftNotes: 6:6 Or in the sap of the mallow plant

units.leftText: My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
units.rightText: My soul refuseth to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.

units.leftText: If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope:
units.rightText: Oh that I might have my request; And that God would grant me the thing that I long for!

units.leftText: that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
units.rightText: Even that it would please God to crush me; That he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

units.leftText: It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
units.rightText: And be it still my consolation, Yea, let me exult in pain that spareth not, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

units.leftText: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
units.rightText: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?

units.leftText: Is my strength like that of stone, or my flesh made of bronze?
units.rightText: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

units.leftText: Is there any help within me now that success is driven from me?
units.rightText: Is it not that I have no help in me, And that wisdom is driven quite from me?

units.leftText: A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
units.rightText: To him that is ready to faint kindness should be showed from his friend; Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

units.leftText: But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow,
units.rightText: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that pass away;

units.leftText: darkened because of the ice and the inflow of melting snow,
units.rightText: Which are black by reason of the ice, And wherein the snow hideth itself:

units.leftText: but ceasing in the dry season and vanishing from their channels in the heat.
units.rightText: What time they wax warm, they vanish; When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

units.leftText: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
units.rightText: The caravans that travel by the way of them turn aside; They go up into the waste, and perish.

units.leftText: The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
units.rightText: The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them.

units.leftText: They are confounded because they had hoped; their arrival brings disappointment.
units.rightText: They were put to shame because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded.

units.leftText: For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.
units.rightText: For now ye are nothing; Ye see a terror, and are afraid.

units.leftText: Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth;
units.rightText: Did I say, Give unto me? Or, Offer a present for me of your substance?

units.leftText: deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’ ?
units.rightText: Or, Deliver me from the adversary’s hand? Or, Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?

units.leftText: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
units.rightText: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

units.leftText: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
units.rightText: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?

units.leftText: Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?
units.rightText: Do ye think to reprove words, Seeing that the speeches of one that is desperate are as wind?

units.leftText: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
units.rightText: Yea, ye would cast lots upon the fatherless, And make merchandise of your friend.

units.leftText: But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
units.rightText: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face.

units.leftText: Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.
units.rightText: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous.

units.leftText: Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?[’’]
units.rightText: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern mischievous things?

units.leftText: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
units.rightText: Is there not a warfare to man upon earth? And are not his days like the days of a hireling?

units.leftText: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.
units.rightText: As a servant that earnestly desireth the shadow, And as a hireling that looketh for his wages:

units.leftText: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed to me.
units.rightText: So am I made to possess months of misery, And wearisome nights are appointed to me.

units.leftText: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
units.rightText: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? And I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.

units.leftText: My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt; my skin is cracked and festering.
units.rightText: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; My skin closeth up, and breaketh out afresh.

units.leftText: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
units.rightText: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, And are spent without hope.

units.leftText: Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
units.rightText: Oh remember that my life is a breath: Mine eye shall no more see good.

units.leftText: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
units.rightText: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more; Thine eyes shall be upon me, but I shall not be.

units.leftText: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
units.rightText: As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away, So he that goeth down to Sheol shall come up no more.

units.leftText: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
units.rightText: He shall return no more to his house, Neither shall his place know him any more.

units.leftText: Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
units.rightText: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.

units.leftText: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?
units.rightText: Am I a sea, or a sea-monster, That thou settest a watch over me?

units.leftText: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
units.rightText: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, My couch shall ease my complaint;

units.leftText: then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
units.rightText: Then thou scarest me with dreams, And terrifiest me through visions:

units.leftText: so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.
units.rightText: So that my soul chooseth strangling, And death rather than these my bones.

units.leftText: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
units.rightText: I loathe my life; I would not live alway: Let me alone; for my days are vanity.

units.leftText: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,
units.rightText: What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him, And that thou shouldest set thy mind upon him,

units.leftText: that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?
units.rightText: And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, And try him every moment?

units.leftText: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?
units.rightText: How long wilt thou not look away from me, Nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?

units.leftText: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?
units.rightText: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?

units.leftText: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
units.rightText: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? For now shall I lie down in the dust; And thou wilt seek me diligently, but I shall not be.

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

units.leftText: “How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.
units.rightText: How long wilt thou speak these things? And how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a mighty wind?

units.leftText: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
units.rightText: Doth God pervert justice? Or doth the Almighty pervert righteousness?

units.leftText: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.
units.rightText: If thy children have sinned against him, And he hath delivered them into the hand of their transgression;

units.leftText: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,
units.rightText: If thou wouldest seek diligently unto God, And make thy supplication to the Almighty;

units.leftText: if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf and restore your righteous estate.
units.rightText: If thou wert pure and upright: Surely now he would awake for thee, And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.

units.leftText: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.
units.rightText: And though thy beginning was small, Yet thy latter end would greatly increase.

units.leftText: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.
units.rightText: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former age, And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out

units.leftText: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
units.rightText: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, Because our days upon earth are a shadow);

units.leftText: Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?
units.rightText: Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, And utter words out of their heart?

units.leftText: Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?
units.rightText: Can the rush grow up without mire? Can the flag grow without water?

units.leftText: While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass.
units.rightText: Whilst it is yet in its greenness, and not cut down, It withereth before any other herb.

units.leftText: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.
units.rightText: So are the paths of all that forget God; And the hope of the godless man shall perish:

units.leftText: His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.
units.rightText: Whose confidence shall break in sunder, And whose trust is a spider’s web.

units.leftText: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.
units.rightText: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: He shall hold fast thereby, but it shall not endure.

units.leftText: He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.
units.rightText: He is green before the sun, And his shoots go forth over his garden.

units.leftText: His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.
units.rightText: His roots are wrapped about the stone-heap, He beholdeth the place of stones.

units.leftText: If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘ I never saw you.’
units.rightText: If he be destroyed from his place, Then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.

units.leftText: Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.
units.rightText: Behold, this is the joy of his way; And out of the earth shall others spring.

units.leftText: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
units.rightText: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, Neither will he uphold the evil-doers.

units.leftText: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
units.rightText: He will yet fill thy mouth with laughter, And thy lips with shouting.

units.leftText: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
units.rightText: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; And the tent of the wicked shall be no more.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
units.rightText: Of a truth I know that it is so: But how can man be just with God?

units.leftText: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
units.rightText: If he be pleased to contend with him, He cannot answer him one of a thousand.
leftNotes: 9:3 Or If God wished to contend with someone

units.leftText: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
units.rightText: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: Who hath hardened himself against him, and prospered?—

units.leftText: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
units.rightText: Him that removeth the mountains, and they know it not, When he overturneth them in his anger;

units.leftText: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
units.rightText: That shaketh the earth out of its place, And the pillars thereof tremble;

units.leftText: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
units.rightText: That commandeth the sun, and it riseth not, And sealeth up the stars;

units.leftText: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
units.rightText: That alone stretcheth out the heavens, And treadeth upon the waves of the sea;

units.leftText: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
units.rightText: That maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, And the chambers of the south;

units.leftText: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
units.rightText: That doeth great things past finding out, Yea, marvellous things without number.

units.leftText: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
units.rightText: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: He passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

units.leftText: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
units.rightText: Behold, he seizeth the prey, who can hinder him? Who will say unto him, What doest thou?

units.leftText: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
units.rightText: God will not withdraw his anger; The helpers of Rahab do stoop under him.

units.leftText: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
units.rightText: How much less shall I answer him, And choose out my words to reason with him?

units.leftText: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
units.rightText: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer; I would make supplication to my judge.

units.leftText: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
units.rightText: If I had called, and he had answered me, Yet would I not believe that he hearkened unto my voice.

units.leftText: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
units.rightText: For he breaketh me with a tempest, And multiplieth my wounds without cause.

units.leftText: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
units.rightText: He will not suffer me to take my breath, But filleth me with bitterness.

units.leftText: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him ?
units.rightText: If we speak of strength, lo, he is mighty! And if of justice, Who, saith he, will summon me?

units.leftText: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
units.rightText: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me: Though I be perfect, it shall prove me perverse.
leftNotes: 9:20 Or He would declare me guilty

units.leftText: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
units.rightText: I am perfect; I regard not myself; I despise my life.

units.leftText: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
units.rightText: It is all one; therefore I say, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

units.leftText: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
units.rightText: If the scourge slay suddenly, He will mock at the trial of the innocent.

units.leftText: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges. If it is not He, then who is it?
units.rightText: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covereth the faces of the judges thereof: If it be not he, who then is it?

units.leftText: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
units.rightText: Now my days are swifter than a post: They flee away, they see no good.

units.leftText: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
units.rightText: They are passed away as the swift ships; As the eagle that swoopeth on the prey.

units.leftText: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’
units.rightText: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad countenance, and be of good cheer;

units.leftText: I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
units.rightText: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

units.leftText: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
units.rightText: I shall be condemned; Why then do I labor in vain?

units.leftText: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
units.rightText: If I wash myself with snow water, And make my hands never so clean;

units.leftText: then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
units.rightText: Yet wilt thou plunge me in the ditch, And mine own clothes shall abhor me.

units.leftText: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
units.rightText: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.

units.leftText: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
units.rightText: There is no umpire betwixt us, That might lay his hand upon us both.

units.leftText: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
units.rightText: Let him take his rod away from me, And let not his terror make me afraid:

units.leftText: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.[’’]
units.rightText: Then would I speak, and not fear him; For I am not so in myself.

units.leftText: “I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
units.rightText: My soul is weary of my life; I will give free course to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

units.leftText: I will say to God: Do not condemn me! Let me know why You prosecute me.
units.rightText: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; Show me wherefore thou contendest with me.

units.leftText: Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands and favor the schemes of the wicked?
units.rightText: Is it good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, That thou shouldest despise the work of thy hands, And shine upon the counsel of the wicked?

units.leftText: Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?
units.rightText: Hast thou eyes of flesh? Or seest thou as man seeth?

units.leftText: Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,
units.rightText: Are thy days as the days of man, Or thy years as man’s days,

units.leftText: that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin —
units.rightText: That thou inquirest after mine iniquity, And searchest after my sin,

units.leftText: though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
units.rightText: Although thou knowest that I am not wicked, And there is none that can deliver out of thy hand?

units.leftText: Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?
units.rightText: Thy hands have framed me and fashioned me Together round about; yet thou dost destroy me.

units.leftText: Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
units.rightText: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast fashioned me as clay; And wilt thou bring me into dust again?

units.leftText: Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
units.rightText: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, And curdled me like cheese?

units.leftText: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
units.rightText: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, And knit me together with bones and sinews.

units.leftText: You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
units.rightText: Thou hast granted me life and lovingkindness; And thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
leftNotes: 10:12 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind:
units.rightText: Yet these things thou didst hide in thy heart; I know that this is with thee:

units.leftText: If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.
units.rightText: If I sin, then thou markest me, And thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.

units.leftText: If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.
units.rightText: If I be wicked, woe unto me; And if I be righteous, yet shall I not lift up my head; Being filled with ignominy, And looking upon mine affliction.

units.leftText: Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion, and again display Your power against me.
units.rightText: And if my head exalt itself, thou huntest me as a lion; And again thou showest thyself marvellous upon me.

units.leftText: You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.
units.rightText: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, And increasest thine indignation upon me: Changes and warfare are with me.

units.leftText: Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!
units.rightText: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me.

units.leftText: If only I had never come to be, but had been carried from the womb to the grave.
units.rightText: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.

units.leftText: Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,
units.rightText: Are not my days few? cease then, And let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,

units.leftText: before I go — never to return — to a land of darkness and gloom,
units.rightText: Before I go whence I shall not return, Even to the land of darkness and of the shadow of death;

units.leftText: to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder, where even the light is like darkness.”
units.rightText: The land dark as midnight, The land of the shadow of death, without any order, And where the light is as midnight.

units.leftText: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

units.leftText: “Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?
units.rightText: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?

units.leftText: Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?
units.rightText: Should thy boastings make men hold their peace? And when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

units.leftText: You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’
units.rightText: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in thine eyes.

units.leftText: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,
units.rightText: But oh that God would speak, And open his lips against thee,

units.leftText: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
units.rightText: And that he would show thee the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding. Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

units.leftText: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?
units.rightText: Canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

units.leftText: They are higher than the heavens— what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol— what can you know?
units.rightText: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do? Deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?

units.leftText: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
units.rightText: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, And broader than the sea.

units.leftText: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?
units.rightText: If he pass through, and shut up, And call unto judgment, then who can hinder him?

units.leftText: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?
units.rightText: For he knoweth false men: He seeth iniquity also, even though he consider it not.

units.leftText: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!
units.rightText: But vain man is void of understanding, Yea, man is born as a wild ass’s colt.

units.leftText: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,
units.rightText: If thou set thy heart aright, And stretch out thy hands toward him;

units.leftText: if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,
units.rightText: If iniquity be in thy hand, put it far away, And let not unrighteousness dwell in thy tents.

units.leftText: then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and unafraid.
units.rightText: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; Yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

units.leftText: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.
units.rightText: For thou shalt forget thy misery; Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away,

units.leftText: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
units.rightText: And thy life shall be clearer than the noonday; Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning.

units.leftText: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.
units.rightText: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; Yea, thou shalt search about thee, and shalt take thy rest in safety.

units.leftText: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.
units.rightText: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; Yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

units.leftText: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
units.rightText: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, And they shall have no way to flee; And their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!
units.rightText: No doubt but ye are the people, And wisdom shall die with you.

units.leftText: But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
units.rightText: But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you: Yea, who knoweth not such things as these?

units.leftText: I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered. The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.
units.rightText: I am as one that is a laughing-stock to his neighbor, I who called upon God, and he answered: The just, the perfect man is a laughing-stock.

units.leftText: The one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
units.rightText: In the thought of him that is at ease there is contempt for misfortune; It is ready for them whose foot slippeth.

units.leftText: The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure — those who carry their god in their hands.
units.rightText: The tents of robbers prosper, And they that provoke God are secure; Into whose hand God bringeth abundantly.
leftNotes: 12:6 Or though God keeps them in His power

units.leftText: But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.
units.rightText: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; And the birds of the heavens, and they shall tell thee:

units.leftText: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.
units.rightText: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee; And the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.

units.leftText: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
units.rightText: Who knoweth not in all these, That the hand of Jehovah hath wrought this,

units.leftText: The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
units.rightText: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?

units.leftText: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?
units.rightText: Doth not the ear try words, Even as the palate tasteth its food?

units.leftText: Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.
units.rightText: With aged men is wisdom, And in length of days understanding.

units.leftText: Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.
units.rightText: With God is wisdom and might; He hath counsel and understanding.

units.leftText: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
units.rightText: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again; He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening.

units.leftText: If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
units.rightText: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up; Again, he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.

units.leftText: True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
units.rightText: With him is strength and wisdom; The deceived and the deceiver are his.

units.leftText: He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.
units.rightText: He leadeth counsellors away stripped, And judges maketh he fools.

units.leftText: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
units.rightText: He looseth the bond of kings, And he bindeth their loins with a girdle.

units.leftText: He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.
units.rightText: He leadeth priests away stripped, And overthroweth the mighty.

units.leftText: He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
units.rightText: He removeth the speech of the trusty, And taketh away the understanding of the elders.

units.leftText: He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
units.rightText: He poureth contempt upon princes, And looseth the belt of the strong.

units.leftText: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.
units.rightText: He uncovereth deep things out of darkness, And bringeth out to light the shadow of death.

units.leftText: He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
units.rightText: He increaseth the nations, and he destroyeth them: He enlargeth the nations, and he leadeth them captive.

units.leftText: He deprives the earth’s leaders of reason and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.
units.rightText: He taketh away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, And causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.

units.leftText: They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.[’’]
units.rightText: They grope in the dark without light; And he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.

units.leftText: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.
units.rightText: Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, Mine ear hath heard and understood it.

units.leftText: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
units.rightText: What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you.

units.leftText: Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.
units.rightText: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason with God.

units.leftText: You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
units.rightText: But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.

units.leftText: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
units.rightText: Oh that ye would altogether hold your peace! And it would be your wisdom.

units.leftText: Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.
units.rightText: Hear now my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.

units.leftText: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
units.rightText: Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?

units.leftText: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?
units.rightText: Will ye show partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?

units.leftText: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him as you would deceive a man?
units.rightText: Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, will ye deceive him?

units.leftText: Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.
units.rightText: He will surely reprove you, If ye do secretly show partiality.

units.leftText: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?
units.rightText: Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?

units.leftText: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
units.rightText: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay.

units.leftText: Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.
units.rightText: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me what will.

units.leftText: Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
units.rightText: Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?
leftNotes: 13:14 Literally Why do I take my flesh in my teeth

units.leftText: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
units.rightText: Behold, he will slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I will maintain my ways before him.
leftNotes: 13:15 Or I have no other hope

units.leftText: Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.
units.rightText: This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.

units.leftText: Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.
units.rightText: Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.

units.leftText: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
units.rightText: Behold now, I have set my cause in order; I know that I am righteous.

units.leftText: Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.
units.rightText: Who is he that will contend with me? For then would I hold my peace and give up the ghost.

units.leftText: Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You:
units.rightText: Only do not two things unto me; Then will I not hide myself from thy face:

units.leftText: Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.
units.rightText: Withdraw thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.

units.leftText: Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.
units.rightText: Then call thou, and I will answer; Or let me speak, and answer thou me.

units.leftText: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.
units.rightText: How many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to know my transgression and my sin.

units.leftText: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?
units.rightText: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?

units.leftText: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?
units.rightText: Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?

units.leftText: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.
units.rightText: For thou writest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:

units.leftText: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
units.rightText: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:

units.leftText: So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.[’’]
units.rightText: Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten.

units.leftText: “Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
units.rightText: Man, that is born of a woman, Is of few days, and full of trouble.

units.leftText: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
units.rightText: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: He fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.

units.leftText: Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?
units.rightText: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, And bringest me into judgment with thee?

units.leftText: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
units.rightText: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.

units.leftText: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,
units.rightText: Seeing his days are determined, The number of his months is with thee, And thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

units.leftText: look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.
units.rightText: Look away from him, that he may rest, Till he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day.

units.leftText: For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its tender shoots will not fail.
units.rightText: For there is hope of a tree, If it be cut down, that it will sprout again, And that the tender branch thereof will not cease.

units.leftText: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,
units.rightText: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, And the stock thereof die in the ground;

units.leftText: at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.
units.rightText: Yet through the scent of water it will bud, And put forth boughs like a plant.

units.leftText: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?
units.rightText: But man dieth, and is laid low: Yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?

units.leftText: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,
units.rightText: As the waters fail from the sea, And the river wasteth and drieth up;

units.leftText: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.
units.rightText: So man lieth down and riseth not: Till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, Nor be roused out of their sleep.

units.leftText: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
units.rightText: Oh that thou wouldest hide me in Sheol, That thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, That thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!

units.leftText: When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes.
units.rightText: If a man die, shall he live again? All the days of my warfare would I wait, Till my release should come.
leftNotes: 14:14 Or my change or my relief

units.leftText: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.
units.rightText: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer thee: Thou wouldest have a desire to the work of thy hands.

units.leftText: For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.
units.rightText: But now thou numberest my steps: Dost thou not watch over my sin?

units.leftText: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
units.rightText: My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And thou fastenest up mine iniquity.

units.leftText: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,
units.rightText: But the mountain falling cometh to nought; And the rock is removed out of its place;

units.leftText: as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil, so You destroy a man’s hope.
units.rightText: The waters wear the stones; The overflowings thereof wash away the dust of the earth: So thou destroyest the hope of man.

units.leftText: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
units.rightText: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth; Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.

units.leftText: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.
units.rightText: His sons come to honor, and he knoweth it not; And they are brought low, but he perceiveth it not of them.

units.leftText: He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”
units.rightText: But his flesh upon him hath pain, And his soul within him mourneth.

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

units.leftText: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
units.rightText: Should a wise man make answer with vain knowledge, And fill himself with the east wind?

units.leftText: Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?
units.rightText: Should he reason with unprofitable talk, Or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?

units.leftText: But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.
units.rightText: Yea, thou doest away with fear, And hinderest devotion before God.

units.leftText: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
units.rightText: For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth, And thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.

units.leftText: Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.
units.rightText: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I; Yea, thine own lips testify against thee.

units.leftText: Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
units.rightText: Art thou the first man that was born? Or wast thou brought forth before the hills?

units.leftText: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?
units.rightText: Hast thou heard the secret counsel of God? And dost thou limit wisdom to thyself?

units.leftText: What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?
units.rightText: What knowest thou, that we know not? What understandest thou, which is not in us?

units.leftText: Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side — men much older than your father.
units.rightText: With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, Much elder than thy father.

units.leftText: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?
units.rightText: Are the consolations of God too small for thee, Even the word that is gentle toward thee?

units.leftText: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,
units.rightText: Why doth thy heart carry thee away? And why do thine eyes flash,

units.leftText: so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?
units.rightText: That against God thou turnest thy spirit, And lettest words go out of thy mouth?

units.leftText: What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
units.rightText: What is man, that he should be clean? And he that is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?

units.leftText: If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,
units.rightText: Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones; Yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight:

units.leftText: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?
units.rightText: How much less one that is abominable and corrupt, A man that drinketh iniquity like water!

units.leftText: Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen,
units.rightText: I will show thee, hear thou me; And that which I have seen I will declare

units.leftText: what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers,
units.rightText: (Which wise men have told From their fathers, and have not hid it;

units.leftText: to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.
units.rightText: Unto whom alone the land was given, And no stranger passed among them):

units.leftText: A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.
units.rightText: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days, Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.

units.leftText: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
units.rightText: A sound of terrors is in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.

units.leftText: He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.
units.rightText: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, And he is waited for of the sword.

units.leftText: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
units.rightText: He wandereth abroad for bread, saying, Where is it? He knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

units.leftText: Distress and anguish terrify him, overwhelming him like a king poised to attack.
units.rightText: Distress and anguish make him afraid; They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.

units.leftText: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty,
units.rightText: Because he hath stretched out his hand against God, And behaveth himself proudly against the Almighty;

units.leftText: rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.
units.rightText: He runneth upon him with a stiff neck, With the thick bosses of his bucklers;

units.leftText: Though his face is covered with fat and his waistline bulges with flesh,
units.rightText: Because he hath covered his face with his fatness, And gathered fat upon his loins;

units.leftText: he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.
units.rightText: And he hath dwelt in desolate cities, In houses which no man inhabited, Which were ready to become heaps;

units.leftText: He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.
units.rightText: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, Neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.

units.leftText: He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.
units.rightText: He shall not depart out of darkness; The flame shall dry up his branches, And by the breath of God’s mouth shall he go away.

units.leftText: Let him not deceive himself with trust in emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.
units.rightText: Let him not trust in vanity, deceiving himself; For vanity shall be his recompense.

units.leftText: It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.
units.rightText: It shall be accomplished before his time, And his branch shall not be green.

units.leftText: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
units.rightText: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, And shall cast off his flower as the olive-tree.

units.leftText: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
units.rightText: For the company of the godless shall be barren, And fire shall consume the tents of bribery.

units.leftText: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”
units.rightText: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity, And their heart prepareth deceit.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
units.rightText: I have heard many such things: Miserable comforters are ye all.

units.leftText: Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
units.rightText: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provoketh thee that thou answerest?

units.leftText: I could also speak like you if you were in my place; I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you.
units.rightText: I also could speak as ye do; If your soul were in my soul’s stead, I could join words together against you, And shake my head at you.

units.leftText: But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.
units.rightText: But I would strengthen you with my mouth, And the solace of my lips would assuage your grief.

units.leftText: Even if I speak, my pain is not relieved, and if I hold back, how will it go away?
