units.rightText: Though I speak, my grief is not assuaged; And though I forbear, what am I eased?

units.leftText: Surely He has now exhausted me; You have devastated all my family.
units.rightText: But now he hath made me weary: Thou hast made desolate all my company.

units.leftText: You have bound me, and it has become a witness; my frailty rises up and testifies against me.
units.rightText: And thou hast laid fast hold on me, which is a witness against me: And my leanness riseth up against me, It testifieth to my face.

units.leftText: His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me. My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
units.rightText: He hath torn me in his wrath, and persecuted me; He hath gnashed upon me with his teeth: Mine adversary sharpeneth his eyes upon me.

units.leftText: They open their mouths against me and strike my cheeks with contempt; they join together against me.
units.rightText: They have gaped upon me with their mouth; They have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully: They gather themselves together against me.

units.leftText: God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.
units.rightText: God delivereth me to the ungodly, And casteth me into the hands of the wicked.

units.leftText: I was at ease, but He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has set me up as His target;
units.rightText: I was at ease, and he brake me asunder; Yea, he hath taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces: He hath also set me up for his mark.

units.leftText: His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without mercy and spills my gall on the ground.
units.rightText: His archers compass me round about; He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; He poureth out my gall upon the ground.

units.leftText: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He rushes me like a mighty warrior.
units.rightText: He breaketh me with breach upon breach; He runneth upon me like a giant.

units.leftText: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin; I have buried my horn in the dust.
units.rightText: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin, And have laid my horn in the dust.

units.leftText: My face is red with weeping, and deep shadows ring my eyes;
units.rightText: My face is red with weeping, And on my eyelids is the shadow of death;

units.leftText: yet my hands are free of violence and my prayer is pure.
units.rightText: Although there is no violence in my hands, And my prayer is pure.

units.leftText: O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry for help never be laid to rest.
units.rightText: O earth, cover not thou my blood, And let my cry have no resting-place.

units.leftText: Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
units.rightText: Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, And he that voucheth for me is on high.

units.leftText: My friends are my scoffers as my eyes pour out tears to God.
units.rightText: My friends scoff at me: But mine eye poureth out tears unto God,

units.leftText: Oh, that a man might plead with God as he pleads with his neighbor!
units.rightText: That he would maintain the right of a man with God, And of a son of man with his neighbor!

units.leftText: For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.[’’]
units.rightText: For when a few years are come, I shall go the way whence I shall not return.

units.leftText: “My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave awaits me.
units.rightText: My spirit is consumed, my days are extinct, The grave is ready for me.

units.leftText: Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must gaze at their rebellion.
units.rightText: Surely there are mockers with me, And mine eye dwelleth upon their provocation.

units.leftText: Give me, I pray, the pledge You demand. Who else will be my guarantor?
units.rightText: Give now a pledge, be surety for me with thyself; Who is there that will strike hands with me?

units.leftText: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
units.rightText: For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: Therefore shalt thou not exalt them.

units.leftText: If a man denounces his friends for a price, the eyes of his children will fail.
units.rightText: He that denounceth his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail.

units.leftText: He has made me a byword among the people, a man in whose face they spit.
units.rightText: But he hath made me a byword of the people; And they spit in my face.

units.leftText: My eyes have grown dim with grief, and my whole body is but a shadow.
units.rightText: Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, And all my members are as a shadow.

units.leftText: The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred against the godless.
units.rightText: Upright men shall be astonished at this, And the innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.

units.leftText: Yet a righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.
units.rightText: Yet shall the righteous hold on his way, And he that hath clean hands shall wax stronger and stronger.

units.leftText: But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.
units.rightText: But as for you all, come on now again; And I shall not find a wise man among you.

units.leftText: My days have passed; my plans are broken off — even the desires of my heart.
units.rightText: My days are past, my purposes are broken off, Even the thoughts of my heart.

units.leftText: They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.
units.rightText: They change the night into day: The light, say they, is near unto the darkness.

units.leftText: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
units.rightText: If I look for Sheol as my house; If I have spread my couch in the darkness;

units.leftText: and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’
units.rightText: If I have said to corruption, Thou art my father; To the worm, Thou art my mother, and my sister;

units.leftText: where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
units.rightText: Where then is my hope? And as for my hope, who shall see it?

units.leftText: Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
units.rightText: It shall go down to the bars of Sheol, When once there is rest in the dust.

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

units.leftText: “How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.
units.rightText: How long will ye hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.

units.leftText: Why are we regarded as cattle, as stupid in your sight?
units.rightText: Wherefore are we counted as beasts, And are become unclean in your sight?

units.leftText: You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account, or the rocks be moved from their place?
units.rightText: Thou that tearest thyself in thine anger, Shall the earth be forsaken for thee? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?

units.leftText: Indeed, the lamp of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire does not glow.
units.rightText: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, And the spark of his fire shall not shine.

units.leftText: The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp beside him goes out.
units.rightText: The light shall be dark in his tent, And his lamp above him shall be put out.

units.leftText: His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up.
units.rightText: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, And his own counsel shall cast him down.

units.leftText: For his own feet lead him into a net, and he wanders into its mesh.
units.rightText: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, And he walketh upon the toils.

units.leftText: A trap seizes his heel; a snare grips him.
units.rightText: A gin shall take him by the heel, And a snare shall lay hold on him.

units.leftText: A noose is hidden in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.
units.rightText: A noose is hid for him in the ground, And a trap for him in the way.

units.leftText: Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.
units.rightText: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, And shall chase him at his heels.

units.leftText: His strength is depleted, and calamity is ready at his side.
units.rightText: His strength shall be hunger-bitten, And calamity shall be ready at his side.

units.leftText: It devours patches of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
units.rightText: The members of his body shall be devoured, Yea, the first-born of death shall devour his members.

units.leftText: He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.
units.rightText: He shall be rooted out of his tent wherein he trusteth; And he shall be brought to the king of terrors.

units.leftText: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling.
units.rightText: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his: Brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.

units.leftText: The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
units.rightText: His roots shall be dried up beneath, And above shall his branch be cut off.

units.leftText: The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.
units.rightText: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, And he shall have no name in the street.

units.leftText: He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.
units.rightText: He shall be driven from light into darkness, And chased out of the world.

units.leftText: He has no offspring or posterity among his people, no survivor where he once lived.
units.rightText: He shall have neither son nor son’s son among his people, Nor any remaining where he sojourned.

units.leftText: Those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror.
units.rightText: They that come after shall be astonished at his day, As they that went before were affrighted.

units.leftText: Surely such is the dwelling of the wicked and the place of one who does not know God.”
units.rightText: Surely such are the dwellings of the unrighteous, And this is the place of him that knoweth not God.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
units.rightText: How long will ye vex my soul, And break me in pieces with words?

units.leftText: Ten times now you have reproached me; you shamelessly mistreat me.
units.rightText: These ten times have ye reproached me: Ye are not ashamed that ye deal hardly with me.

units.leftText: Even if I have truly gone astray, my error concerns me alone.
units.rightText: And be it indeed that I have erred, Mine error remaineth with myself.

units.leftText: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my disgrace against me,
units.rightText: If indeed ye will magnify yourselves against me, And plead against me my reproach;

units.leftText: then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
units.rightText: Know now that God hath subverted me in my cause, And hath compassed me with his net.

units.leftText: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
units.rightText: Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry for help, but there is no justice.

units.leftText: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.
units.rightText: He hath walled up my way that I cannot pass, And hath set darkness in my paths.

units.leftText: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
units.rightText: He hath stripped me of my glory, And taken the crown from my head.

units.leftText: He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
units.rightText: He hath broken me down on every side, and I am gone; And my hope hath he plucked up like a tree.

units.leftText: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
units.rightText: He hath also kindled his wrath against me, And he counteth me unto him as one of his adversaries.

units.leftText: His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me and encamp around my tent.
units.rightText: His troops come on together, And cast up their way against me, And encamp round about my tent.

units.leftText: He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me.
units.rightText: He hath put my brethren far from me, And mine acquaintance are wholly estranged from me.

units.leftText: My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.
units.rightText: My kinsfolk have failed, And my familiar friends have forgotten me.

units.leftText: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.
units.rightText: They that dwell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.

units.leftText: I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.
units.rightText: I call unto my servant, and he giveth me no answer, Though I entreat him with my mouth.

units.leftText: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family.
units.rightText: My breath is strange to my wife, And my supplication to the children of mine own mother.

units.leftText: Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.
units.rightText: Even young children despise me; If I arise, they speak against me.

units.leftText: All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me.
units.rightText: All my familiar friends abhor me, And they whom I loved are turned against me.

units.leftText: My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
units.rightText: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, And I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.

units.leftText: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
units.rightText: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; For the hand of God hath touched me.

units.leftText: Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
units.rightText: Why do ye persecute me as God, And are not satisfied with my flesh?

units.leftText: I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book,
units.rightText: Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!

units.leftText: by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.
units.rightText: That with an iron pen and lead They were graven in the rock for ever!

units.leftText: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
units.rightText: But as for me I know that my Redeemer liveth, And at last he will stand up upon the earth:

units.leftText: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
units.rightText: And after my skin, even this body, is destroyed, Then without my flesh shall I see God;

units.leftText: I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger. How my heart yearns within me!
units.rightText: Whom I, even I, shall see, on my side, And mine eyes shall behold, and not as a stranger. My heart is consumed within me.

units.leftText: If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him, ’
units.rightText: If ye say, How we will persecute him! And that the root of the matter is found in me;
leftNotes: 19:28 Many Hebrew manuscripts, LXX, and Vulgate; most Hebrew manuscripts with me

units.leftText: then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment.”
units.rightText: Be ye afraid of the sword: For wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword, That ye may know there is a judgment.

units.leftText: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

units.leftText: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
units.rightText: Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me, Even by reason of my haste that is in me.

units.leftText: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.
units.rightText: I have heard the reproof which putteth me to shame; And the spirit of my understanding answereth me.

units.leftText: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,
units.rightText: Knowest thou not this of old time, Since man was placed upon earth,

units.leftText: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
units.rightText: That the triumphing of the wicked is short, And the joy of the godless but for a moment?

units.leftText: Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,
units.rightText: Though his height mount up to the heavens, And his head reach unto the clouds;

units.leftText: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’
units.rightText: Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: They that have seen him shall say, Where is he?

units.leftText: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
units.rightText: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: Yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.

units.leftText: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
units.rightText: The eye which saw him shall see him no more; Neither shall his place any more behold him.

units.leftText: His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
units.rightText: His children shall seek the favor of the poor, And his hands shall give back his wealth.

units.leftText: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
units.rightText: His bones are full of his youth, But it shall lie down with him in the dust.

units.leftText: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,
units.rightText: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, Though he hide it under his tongue,

units.leftText: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,
units.rightText: Though he spare it, and will not let it go, But keep it still within his mouth;

units.leftText: yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.
units.rightText: Yet his food in his bowels is turned, It is the gall of asps within him.

units.leftText: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.
units.rightText: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again; God will cast them out of his belly.

units.leftText: He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.
units.rightText: He shall suck the poison of asps: The viper’s tongue shall slay him.

units.leftText: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
units.rightText: He shall not look upon the rivers, The flowing streams of honey and butter.

units.leftText: He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.
units.rightText: That which he labored for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down; According to the substance that he hath gotten, he shall not rejoice.

units.leftText: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
units.rightText: For he hath oppressed and forsaken the poor; He hath violently taken away a house, and he shall not build it up.

units.leftText: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
units.rightText: Because he knew no quietness within him, He shall not save aught of that wherein he delighteth.

units.leftText: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
units.rightText: There was nothing left that he devoured not; Therefore his prosperity shall not endure.

units.leftText: In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.
units.rightText: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: The hand of every one that is in misery shall come upon him.

units.leftText: When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him, raining it down on him as he eats.
units.rightText: When he is about to fill his belly, God will cast the fierceness of his wrath upon him, And will rain it upon him while he is eating.

units.leftText: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
units.rightText: He shall flee from the iron weapon, And the bow of brass shall strike him through.

units.leftText: It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver. Terrors come over him.
units.rightText: He draweth it forth, and it cometh out of his body; Yea, the glittering point cometh out of his gall: Terrors are upon him.

units.leftText: Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him and devour what is left in his tent.
units.rightText: All darkness is laid up for his treasures: A fire not blown by man shall devour him; It shall consume that which is left in his tent.

units.leftText: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
units.rightText: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, And the earth shall rise up against him.

units.leftText: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
units.rightText: The increase of his house shall depart; His goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.

units.leftText: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
units.rightText: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, And the heritage appointed unto him by God.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.
units.rightText: Hear diligently my speech; And let this be your consolations.

units.leftText: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
units.rightText: Suffer me, and I also will speak; And after that I have spoken, mock on.

units.leftText: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?
units.rightText: As for me, is my complaint to man? And why should I not be impatient?

units.leftText: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
units.rightText: Mark me, and be astonished, And lay your hand upon your mouth.

units.leftText: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.
units.rightText: Even when I remember I am troubled, And horror taketh hold on my flesh.

units.leftText: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
units.rightText: Wherefore do the wicked live, Become old, yea, wax mighty in power?

units.leftText: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
units.rightText: Their seed is established with them in their sight, And their offspring before their eyes.

units.leftText: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.
units.rightText: Their houses are safe from fear, Neither is the rod of God upon them.

units.leftText: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.
units.rightText: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; Their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

units.leftText: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
units.rightText: They send forth their little ones like a flock, And their children dance.

units.leftText: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
units.rightText: They sing to the timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of the pipe.

units.leftText: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
units.rightText: They spend their days in prosperity, And in a moment they go down to Sheol.

units.leftText: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
units.rightText: And they say unto God, Depart from us; For we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

units.leftText: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
units.rightText: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? And what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

units.leftText: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
units.rightText: Lo, their prosperity is not in their hand: The counsel of the wicked is far from me.

units.leftText: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
units.rightText: How oft is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out? That their calamity cometh upon them? That God distributeth sorrows in his anger?

units.leftText: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
units.rightText: That they are as stubble before the wind, And as chaff that the storm carrieth away?

units.leftText: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.
units.rightText: Ye say, God layeth up his iniquity for his children. Let him recompense it unto himself, that he may know it:

units.leftText: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.
units.rightText: Let his own eyes see his destruction, And let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

units.leftText: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?
units.rightText: For what careth he for his house after him, When the number of his months is cut off?

units.leftText: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
units.rightText: Shall any teach God knowledge, Seeing he judgeth those that are high?

units.leftText: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.
units.rightText: One dieth in his full strength, Being wholly at ease and quiet:

units.leftText: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
units.rightText: His pails are full of milk, And the marrow of his bones is moistened.
leftNotes: 21:24 Literally His pails are full of milk

units.leftText: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
units.rightText: And another dieth in bitterness of soul, And never tasteth of good.

units.leftText: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
units.rightText: They lie down alike in the dust, And the worm covereth them.

units.leftText: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
units.rightText: Behold, I know your thoughts, And the devices wherewith ye would wrong me.

units.leftText: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’
units.rightText: For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? And where is the tent wherein the wicked dwelt?

units.leftText: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?
units.rightText: Have ye not asked wayfaring men? And do ye not know their evidences,

units.leftText: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
units.rightText: That the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity? That they are led forth to the day of wrath?

units.leftText: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
units.rightText: Who shall declare his way to his face? And who shall repay him what he hath done?

units.leftText: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
units.rightText: Yet shall he be borne to the grave, And men shall keep watch over the tomb.

units.leftText: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.
units.rightText: The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, And all men shall draw after him, As there were innumerable before him.

units.leftText: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”
units.rightText: How then comfort ye me in vain, Seeing in your answers there remaineth only falsehood?

units.leftText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,

units.leftText: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
units.rightText: Can a man be profitable unto God? Surely he that is wise is profitable unto himself.

units.leftText: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
units.rightText: Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? Or is it gain to him, that thou makest thy ways perfect?

units.leftText: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
units.rightText: Is it for thy fear of him that he reproveth thee, That he entereth with thee into judgment?

units.leftText: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
units.rightText: Is not thy wickedness great? Neither is there any end to thine iniquities.

units.leftText: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
units.rightText: For thou hast taken pledges of thy brother for nought, And stripped the naked of their clothing.

units.leftText: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,
units.rightText: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, And thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.

units.leftText: while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.
units.rightText: But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; And the honorable man, he dwelt in it.

units.leftText: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
units.rightText: Thou hast sent widows away empty, And the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

units.leftText: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
units.rightText: Therefore snares are round about thee, And sudden fear troubleth thee,

units.leftText: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
units.rightText: Or darkness, so that thou canst not see, And abundance of waters cover thee.

units.leftText: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
units.rightText: Is not God in the height of heaven? And behold the height of the stars, how high they are!

units.leftText: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?
units.rightText: And thou sayest, What doth God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?

units.leftText: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven. ’
units.rightText: Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he seeth not; And he walketh on the vault of heaven.
leftNotes: 22:14 Or heaven’s horizon or the circle of the sky

units.leftText: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?
units.rightText: Wilt thou keep the old way Which wicked men have trodden?

units.leftText: They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.
units.rightText: Who were snatched away before their time, Whose foundation was poured out as a stream,

units.leftText: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’
units.rightText: Who said unto God, Depart from us; And, What can the Almighty do for us?

units.leftText: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
units.rightText: Yet he filled their houses with good things: But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

units.leftText: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
units.rightText: The righteous see it, and are glad; And the innocent laugh them to scorn,

units.leftText: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’
units.rightText: Saying, Surely they that did rise up against us are cut off, And the remnant of them the fire hath consumed.

units.leftText: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
units.rightText: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: Thereby good shall come unto thee.

units.leftText: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
units.rightText: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, And lay up his words in thy heart.

units.leftText: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents
units.rightText: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, If thou put away unrighteousness far from thy tents.

units.leftText: and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,
units.rightText: And lay thou thy treasure in the dust, And the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks;

units.leftText: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.
units.rightText: And the Almighty will be thy treasure, And precious silver unto thee.

units.leftText: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
units.rightText: For then shalt thou delight thyself in the Almighty, And shalt lift up thy face unto God.

units.leftText: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
units.rightText: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he will hear thee; And thou shalt pay thy vows.

units.leftText: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
units.rightText: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee; And light shall shine upon thy ways.

units.leftText: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
units.rightText: When they cast thee down, thou shalt say, There is lifting up; And the humble person he will save.

units.leftText: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
units.rightText: He will deliver even him that is not innocent: Yea, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of thy hands.

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
units.rightText: Even to-day is my complaint rebellious: My stroke is heavier than my groaning.

units.leftText: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
units.rightText: Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!

units.leftText: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
units.rightText: I would set my cause in order before him, And fill my mouth with arguments.

units.leftText: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
units.rightText: I would know the words which he would answer me, And understand what he would say unto me.

units.leftText: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
units.rightText: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? Nay; but he would give heed unto me.

units.leftText: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
units.rightText: There the upright might reason with him; So should I be delivered for ever from my judge.

units.leftText: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
units.rightText: Behold, I go forward, but he is not there; And backward, but I cannot perceive him;

units.leftText: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
units.rightText: On the left hand, when he doth work, but I cannot behold him; He hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him.

units.leftText: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
units.rightText: But he knoweth the way that I take; When he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

units.leftText: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.
units.rightText: My foot hath held fast to his steps; His way have I kept, and turned not aside.

units.leftText: I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth more than my daily bread.
units.rightText: I have not gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured up the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.

units.leftText: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
units.rightText: But he is in one mind, and who can turn him? And what his soul desireth, even that he doeth.

units.leftText: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
units.rightText: For he performeth that which is appointed for me: And many such things are with him.

units.leftText: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.
units.rightText: Therefore am I terrified at his presence; When I consider, I am afraid of him.

units.leftText: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
units.rightText: For God hath made my heart faint, And the Almighty hath terrified me;

units.leftText: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.[’’]
units.rightText: Because I was not cut off before the darkness, Neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face.

units.leftText: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
units.rightText: Why are times not laid up by the Almighty? And why do not they that know him see his days?

units.leftText: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
units.rightText: There are that remove the landmarks; They violently take away flocks, and feed them.

units.leftText: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
units.rightText: They drive away the ass of the fatherless; They take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

units.leftText: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
units.rightText: They turn the needy out of the way: The poor of the earth all hide themselves.

units.leftText: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.
units.rightText: Behold, as wild asses in the desert They go forth to their work, seeking diligently for food; The wilderness yieldeth them bread for their children.

units.leftText: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
units.rightText: They cut their provender in the field; And they glean the vintage of the wicked.

units.leftText: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
units.rightText: They lie all night naked without clothing, And have no covering in the cold.

units.leftText: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
units.rightText: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, And embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

units.leftText: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
units.rightText: There are that pluck the fatherless from the breast, And take a pledge of the poor;

units.leftText: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
units.rightText: So that they go about naked without clothing, And being hungry they carry the sheaves.

units.leftText: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
units.rightText: They make oil within the walls of these men; They tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.

units.leftText: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
units.rightText: From out of the populous city men groan, And the soul of the wounded crieth out: Yet God regardeth not the folly.

units.leftText: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.
units.rightText: These are of them that rebel against the light; They know not the ways thereof, Nor abide in the paths thereof.

units.leftText: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.
units.rightText: The murderer riseth with the light; He killeth the poor and needy; And in the night he is as a thief.

units.leftText: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.
units.rightText: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, Saying, No eye shall see me: And he disguiseth his face.

units.leftText: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.
units.rightText: In the dark they dig through houses: They shut themselves up in the day-time; They know not the light.

units.leftText: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!
units.rightText: For the morning is to all of them as thick darkness; For they know the terrors of the thick darkness.

units.leftText: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
units.rightText: Swiftly they pass away upon the face of the waters; Their portion is cursed in the earth: They turn not into the way of the vineyards.

units.leftText: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
units.rightText: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: So doth Sheol those that have sinned.

units.leftText: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.
units.rightText: The womb shall forget him; The worm shall feed sweetly on him; He shall be no more remembered; And unrighteousness shall be broken as a tree.

units.leftText: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
units.rightText: He devoureth the barren that beareth not, And doeth not good to the widow.

units.leftText: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
units.rightText: Yet God preserveth the mighty by his power: He riseth up that hath no assurance of life.

units.leftText: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
units.rightText: God giveth them to be in security, and they rest thereon; And his eyes are upon their ways.

units.leftText: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
units.rightText: They are exalted; yet a little while, and they are gone; Yea, they are brought low, they are taken out of the way as all others, And are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.

units.leftText: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
units.rightText: And if it be not so now, who will prove me a liar, And make my speech nothing worth?

units.leftText: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
units.rightText: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

units.leftText: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
units.rightText: Dominion and fear are with him; He maketh peace in his high places.

units.leftText: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
units.rightText: Is there any number of his armies? And upon whom doth not his light arise?

units.leftText: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
units.rightText: How then can man be just with God? Or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?

units.leftText: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,
units.rightText: Behold, even the moon hath no brightness, And the stars are not pure in his sight:

units.leftText: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
units.rightText: How much less man, that is a worm! And the son of man, that is a worm!

units.leftText: Then Job answered:
units.rightText: Then Job answered and said,

units.leftText: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!
units.rightText: How hast thou helped him that is without power! How hast thou saved the arm that hath no strength!

units.leftText: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!
units.rightText: How hast thou counselled him that hath no wisdom, And plentifully declared sound knowledge!

units.leftText: To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?
units.rightText: To whom hast thou uttered words? And whose spirit came forth from thee?

units.leftText: The dead tremble — those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
units.rightText: They that are deceased tremble Beneath the waters and the inhabitants thereof.

units.leftText: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
units.rightText: Sheol is naked before God, And Abaddon hath no covering.

units.leftText: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing.
units.rightText: He stretcheth out the north over empty space, And hangeth the earth upon nothing.

units.leftText: He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.
units.rightText: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; And the cloud is not rent under them.

units.leftText: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud.
units.rightText: He incloseth the face of his throne, And spreadeth his cloud upon it.

units.leftText: He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.
units.rightText: He hath described a boundary upon the face of the waters, Unto the confines of light and darkness.

units.leftText: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke.
units.rightText: The pillars of heaven tremble And are astonished at his rebuke.

units.leftText: By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
units.rightText: He stirreth up the sea with his power, And by his understanding he smiteth through Rahab.

units.leftText: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
units.rightText: By his Spirit the heavens are garnished; His hand hath pierced the swift serpent.
leftNotes: 26:13 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake

units.leftText: Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”
units.rightText: Lo, these are but the outskirts of his ways: And how small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?

units.leftText: Job continued his discourse:
units.rightText: And Job again took up his parable, and said,

units.leftText: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice — the Almighty, who has embittered my soul —
units.rightText: As God liveth, who hath taken away my right, And the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul

units.leftText: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
units.rightText: (For my life is yet whole in me, And the spirit of God is in my nostrils);

units.leftText: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
units.rightText: Surely my lips shall not speak unrighteousness, Neither shall my tongue utter deceit.

units.leftText: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
units.rightText: Far be it from me that I should justify you: Till I die I will not put away mine integrity from me.

units.leftText: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me. The Wicked Man’s Portion
units.rightText: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live.

units.leftText: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
units.rightText: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, And let him that riseth up against me be as the unrighteous.

units.leftText: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
units.rightText: For what is the hope of the godless, though he get him gain, When God taketh away his soul?

units.leftText: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
units.rightText: Will God hear his cry, When trouble cometh upon him?

units.leftText: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
units.rightText: Will he delight himself in the Almighty, And call upon God at all times?

units.leftText: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.
units.rightText: I will teach you concerning the hand of God; That which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.

units.leftText: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?
units.rightText: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; Why then are ye become altogether vain?

units.leftText: This is the wicked man’s portion from God — the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.
units.rightText: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, And the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty:

units.leftText: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.
units.rightText: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword; And his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

units.leftText: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.
units.rightText: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death, And his widows shall make no lamentation.

units.leftText: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
units.rightText: Though he heap up silver as the dust, And prepare raiment as the clay;

units.leftText: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.
units.rightText: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, And the innocent shall divide the silver.

units.leftText: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
units.rightText: He buildeth his house as the moth, And as a booth which the keeper maketh.

units.leftText: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
units.rightText: He lieth down rich, but he shall not be gathered to his fathers; He openeth his eyes, and he is not.

units.leftText: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
units.rightText: Terrors overtake him like waters; A tempest stealeth him away in the night.

units.leftText: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
units.rightText: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth; And it sweepeth him out of his place.

units.leftText: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
units.rightText: For God shall hurl at him, and not spare: He would fain flee out of his hand.

units.leftText: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.[’’]
units.rightText: Men shall clap their hands at him, And shall hiss him out of his place.

units.leftText: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
units.rightText: Surely there is a mine for silver, And a place for gold which they refine.

units.leftText: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
units.rightText: Iron is taken out of the earth, And copper is molten out of the stone.

units.leftText: Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness.
units.rightText: Man setteth an end to darkness, And searcheth out, to the furthest bound, The stones of obscurity and of thick darkness.

units.leftText: Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.
units.rightText: He breaketh open a shaft away from where men sojourn; They are forgotten of the foot; They hang afar from men, they swing to and fro.

units.leftText: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.
units.rightText: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread; And underneath it is turned up as it were by fire.

units.leftText: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.
units.rightText: The stones thereof are the place of sapphires, And it hath dust of gold.

units.leftText: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
units.rightText: That path no bird of prey knoweth, Neither hath the falcon’s eye seen it:

units.leftText: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.
units.rightText: The proud beasts have not trodden it, Nor hath the fierce lion passed thereby.

units.leftText: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.
units.rightText: He putteth forth his hand upon the flinty rock; He overturneth the mountains by the roots.

units.leftText: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
units.rightText: He cutteth out channels among the rocks; And his eye seeth every precious thing.

units.leftText: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
units.rightText: He bindeth the streams that they trickle not; And the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light.
leftNotes: 28:11 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate He searches

units.leftText: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
units.rightText: But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?

units.leftText: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
units.rightText: Man knoweth not the price thereof; Neither is it found in the land of the living.

units.leftText: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’
units.rightText: The deep saith, It is not in me; And the sea saith, It is not with me.

units.leftText: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
units.rightText: It cannot be gotten for gold, Neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.

units.leftText: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
units.rightText: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, With the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

units.leftText: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.
units.rightText: Gold and glass cannot equal it, Neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.

units.leftText: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
units.rightText: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal: Yea, the price of wisdom is above rubies.

units.leftText: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
units.rightText: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
leftNotes: 28:19 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: From where, then, does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
units.rightText: Whence then cometh wisdom? And where is the place of understanding?

units.leftText: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
units.rightText: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, And kept close from the birds of the heavens.

units.leftText: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’
units.rightText: Destruction and Death say, We have heard a rumor thereof with our ears.

units.leftText: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
units.rightText: God understandeth the way thereof, And he knoweth the place thereof.

units.leftText: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
units.rightText: For he looketh to the ends of the earth, And seeth under the whole heaven;

units.leftText: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
units.rightText: To make a weight for the wind: Yea, he meteth out the waters by measure.

units.leftText: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
units.rightText: When he made a decree for the rain, And a way for the lightning of the thunder;

units.leftText: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.
units.rightText: Then did he see it, and declare it; He established it, yea, and searched it out.

units.leftText: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”
units.rightText: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; And to depart from evil is understanding.

units.leftText: And Job continued his discourse:
units.rightText: And Job again took up his parable, and said,

units.leftText: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
units.rightText: Oh that I were as in the months of old, As in the days when God watched over me;

units.leftText: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
units.rightText: When his lamp shined upon my head, And by his light I walked through darkness;

units.leftText: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
units.rightText: As I was in the ripeness of my days, When the friendship of God was upon my tent;
leftNotes: 29:4 Hebrew in the time of my harvest

units.leftText: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
units.rightText: When the Almighty was yet with me, And my children were about me;

units.leftText: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
units.rightText: When my steps were washed with butter, And the rock poured me out streams of oil!

units.leftText: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
units.rightText: When I went forth to the gate unto the city, When I prepared my seat in the street,

units.leftText: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
units.rightText: The young men saw me and hid themselves, And the aged rose up and stood;

units.leftText: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
units.rightText: The princes refrained from talking, And laid their hand on their mouth;

units.leftText: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
units.rightText: The voice of the nobles was hushed, And their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.

units.leftText: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
units.rightText: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; And when the eye saw me, it gave witness unto me:

units.leftText: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
units.rightText: Because I delivered the poor that cried, The fatherless also, that had none to help him.

units.leftText: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
units.rightText: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me; And I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

units.leftText: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
units.rightText: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: My justice was as a robe and a diadem.

units.leftText: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
units.rightText: I was eyes to the blind, And feet was I to the lame.

units.leftText: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
units.rightText: I was a father to the needy: And the cause of him that I knew not I searched out.

units.leftText: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
units.rightText: And I brake the jaws of the unrighteous, And plucked the prey out of his teeth.

units.leftText: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
units.rightText: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, And I shall multiply my days as the sand:

units.leftText: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
units.rightText: My root is spread out to the waters, And the dew lieth all night upon my branch:

units.leftText: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
units.rightText: My glory is fresh in me, And my bow is renewed in my hand.

units.leftText: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
units.rightText: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, And kept silence for my counsel.

units.leftText: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
units.rightText: After my words they spake not again; And my speech distilled upon them.

units.leftText: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
units.rightText: And they waited for me as for the rain; And they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.

units.leftText: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
units.rightText: I smiled on them, when they had no confidence; And the light of my countenance they cast not down.

units.leftText: I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops, as a comforter of the mourners.[’’]
units.rightText: I chose out their way, and sat as chief, And dwelt as a king in the army, As one that comforteth the mourners.

units.leftText: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs.
units.rightText: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, Whose fathers I disdained to set with the dogs of my flock.

units.leftText: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?
units.rightText: Yea, the strength of their hands, whereto should it profit me? Men in whom ripe age is perished.

units.leftText: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.
units.rightText: They are gaunt with want and famine; They gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of wasteness and desolation.

units.leftText: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.
units.rightText: They pluck salt-wort by the bushes; And the roots of the broom are their food.

units.leftText: They were banished from among men, shouted at like thieves,
units.rightText: They are driven forth from the midst of men; They cry after them as after a thief;

units.leftText: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
units.rightText: So that they dwell in frightful valleys, In holes of the earth and of the rocks.

units.leftText: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.
units.rightText: Among the bushes they bray; Under the nettles they are gathered together.

units.leftText: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.
units.rightText: They are children of fools, yea, children of base men; They were scourged out of the land.

units.leftText: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
units.rightText: And now I am become their song, Yea, I am a byword unto them.

units.leftText: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
units.rightText: They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, And spare not to spit in my face.

units.leftText: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
units.rightText: For he hath loosed his cord, and afflicted me; And they have cast off the bridle before me.

units.leftText: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.
units.rightText: Upon my right hand rise the rabble; They thrust aside my feet, And they cast up against me their ways of destruction.

units.leftText: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.
units.rightText: They mar my path, They set forward my calamity, Even men that have no helper.
leftNotes: 30:13 Or with no one to assist them

units.leftText: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in. Job’s Prosperity Becomes Calamity
units.rightText: As through a wide breach they come: In the midst of the ruin they roll themselves upon me.

units.leftText: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
units.rightText: Terrors are turned upon me; They chase mine honor as the wind; And my welfare is passed away as a cloud.

units.leftText: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.
units.rightText: And now my soul is poured out within me; Days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

units.leftText: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.
units.rightText: In the night season my bones are pierced in me, And the pains that gnaw me take no rest.

units.leftText: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
units.rightText: By God’s great force is my garment disfigured; It bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
leftNotes: 30:18 LXX; Hebrew He becomes like a garment to me or my garment is disfigured

units.leftText: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
units.rightText: He hath cast me into the mire, And I am become like dust and ashes.

units.leftText: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
units.rightText: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not answer me: I stand up, and thou gazest at me.

units.leftText: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
units.rightText: Thou art turned to be cruel to me; With the might of thy hand thou persecutest me.

units.leftText: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.
units.rightText: Thou liftest me up to the wind, thou causest me to ride upon it; And thou dissolvest me in the storm.

units.leftText: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
units.rightText: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, And to the house appointed for all living.

units.leftText: Yet no one stretches out his hand against a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.
units.rightText: Howbeit doth not one stretch out the hand in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?

units.leftText: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
units.rightText: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? Was not my soul grieved for the needy?

units.leftText: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
units.rightText: When I looked for good, then evil came; And when I waited for light, there came darkness.

units.leftText: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.
units.rightText: My heart is troubled, and resteth not; Days of affliction are come upon me.

units.leftText: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
units.rightText: I go mourning without the sun: I stand up in the assembly, and cry for help.

units.leftText: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
units.rightText: I am a brother to jackals, And a companion to ostriches.
leftNotes: 30:29 Literally of daughters of an ostrich or of daughters of an owl

units.leftText: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
units.rightText: My skin is black, and falleth from me, And my bones are burned with heat.

units.leftText: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.[’’]
units.rightText: Therefore is my harp turned to mourning, And my pipe into the voice of them that weep.

units.leftText: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
units.rightText: I made a covenant with mine eyes; How then should I look upon a virgin?

units.leftText: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?
units.rightText: For what is the portion from God above, And the heritage from the Almighty on high?

units.leftText: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
units.rightText: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, And disaster to the workers of iniquity?

units.leftText: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
units.rightText: Doth not he see my ways, And number all my steps?

units.leftText: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,
units.rightText: If I have walked with falsehood, And my foot hath hasted to deceit

units.leftText: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.
units.rightText: (Let me be weighed in an even balance, That God may know mine integrity);

units.leftText: If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,
units.rightText: If my step hath turned out of the way, And my heart walked after mine eyes, And if any spot hath cleaved to my hands:

units.leftText: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
units.rightText: Then let me sow, and let another eat; Yea, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

units.leftText: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,
units.rightText: If my heart hath been enticed unto a woman, And I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door;

units.leftText: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.
units.rightText: Then let my wife grind unto another, And let others bow down upon her.

units.leftText: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.
units.rightText: For that were a heinous crime; Yea, it were an iniquity to be punished by the judges:

units.leftText: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.
units.rightText: For it is a fire that consumeth unto Destruction, And would root out all mine increase.

units.leftText: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,
units.rightText: If I have despised the cause of my man-servant or of my maid-servant, When they contended with me;

units.leftText: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?
units.rightText: What then shall I do when God riseth up? And when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

units.leftText: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?
units.rightText: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? And did not one fashion us in the womb?

units.leftText: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,
units.rightText: If I have withheld the poor from their desire, Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

units.leftText: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless —
units.rightText: Or have eaten my morsel alone, And the fatherless hath not eaten thereof

units.leftText: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow —
units.rightText: (Nay, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And her have I guided from my mother’s womb);

units.leftText: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,
units.rightText: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, Or that the needy had no covering;

units.leftText: if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,
units.rightText: If his loins have not blessed me, And if he hath not been warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
leftNotes: 31:20 Hebrew if his loins have not blessed me

units.leftText: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate,
units.rightText: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, Because I saw my help in the gate:

units.leftText: then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.
units.rightText: Then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder-blade, And mine arm be broken from the bone.

units.leftText: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
units.rightText: For calamity from God is a terror to me, And by reason of his majesty I can do nothing.

units.leftText: If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security,
units.rightText: If I have made gold my hope, And have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence;

units.leftText: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much,
units.rightText: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, And because my hand had gotten much;

units.leftText: if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,
units.rightText: If I have beheld the sun when it shined, Or the moon walking in brightness,

units.leftText: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
units.rightText: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, And my mouth hath kissed my hand:

units.leftText: this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
units.rightText: This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judges; For I should have denied the God that is above.

units.leftText: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him —
units.rightText: If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, Or lifted up myself when evil found him

units.leftText: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse —
units.rightText: (Yea, I have not suffered my mouth to sin By asking his life with a curse);

units.leftText: if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’—
units.rightText: If the men of my tent have not said, Who can find one that hath not been filled with his meat?

units.leftText: but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler —
units.rightText: (The sojourner hath not lodged in the street; But I have opened my doors to the traveller);

units.leftText: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart,
units.rightText: If like Adam I have covered my transgressions, By hiding mine iniquity in my bosom,

units.leftText: because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside —
units.rightText: Because I feared the great multitude, And the contempt of families terrified me, So that I kept silence, and went not out of the door—

units.leftText: (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment.
units.rightText: Oh that I had one to hear me! (Lo, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me) And that I had the indictment which mine adversary hath written!

units.leftText: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
units.rightText: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder; I would bind it unto me as a crown:

units.leftText: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)—
units.rightText: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; As a prince would I go near unto him.

units.leftText: if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
units.rightText: If my land crieth out against me, And the furrows thereof weep together;

units.leftText: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,
units.rightText: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, Or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

units.leftText: then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” Thus conclude the words of Job.
units.rightText: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, And cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

units.leftText: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
units.rightText: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

units.leftText: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
units.rightText: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

units.leftText: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
units.rightText: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

units.leftText: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
units.rightText: Now Elihu had waited to speak unto Job, because they were elder than he.

units.leftText: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
units.rightText: And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.

units.leftText: So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared: “I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.
units.rightText: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I am young, and ye are very old; Wherefore I held back, and durst not show you mine opinion.

units.leftText: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
units.rightText: I said, Days should speak, And multitude of years should teach wisdom.

units.leftText: But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
units.rightText: But there is a spirit in man, And the breath of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
leftNotes: 32:8 Or the Spirit; similarly in verse 18

units.leftText: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.
units.rightText: It is not the great that are wise, Nor the aged that understand justice.

units.leftText: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’
units.rightText: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will show mine opinion.

units.leftText: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words,
units.rightText: Behold, I waited for your words, I listened for your reasonings, Whilst ye searched out what to say.

units.leftText: I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.
units.rightText: Yea, I attended unto you, And, behold, there was none that convinced Job, Or that answered his words, among you.

units.leftText: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’
