units.rightText: Beware lest ye say, We have found wisdom; God may vanquish him, not man:

units.leftText: But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
units.rightText: For he hath not directed his words against me; Neither will I answer him with your speeches.

units.leftText: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them.
units.rightText: They are amazed, they answer no more: They have not a word to say.

units.leftText: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?
units.rightText: And shall I wait, because they speak not, Because they stand still, and answer no more?

units.leftText: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.
units.rightText: I also will answer my part, I also will show mine opinion.

units.leftText: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.
units.rightText: For I am full of words; The spirit within me constraineth me.

units.leftText: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
units.rightText: Behold, my breast is as wine which hath no vent; Like new wine-skins it is ready to burst.

units.leftText: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
units.rightText: I will speak, that I may be refreshed; I will open my lips and answer.

units.leftText: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
units.rightText: Let me not, I pray you, respect any man’s person; Neither will I give flattering titles unto any man.

units.leftText: For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.[’’]
units.rightText: For I know not to give flattering titles; Else would my Maker soon take me away.

units.leftText: “But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
units.rightText: Howbeit, Job, I pray thee, hear my speech, And hearken to all my words.

units.leftText: Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
units.rightText: Behold now, I have opened my mouth; My tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

units.leftText: My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.
units.rightText: My words shall utter the uprightness of my heart; And that which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.

units.leftText: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
units.rightText: The Spirit of God hath made me, And the breath of the Almighty giveth me life.

units.leftText: Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me.
units.rightText: If thou canst, answer thou me; Set thy words in order before me, stand forth.

units.leftText: I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.
units.rightText: Behold, I am toward God even as thou art: I also am formed out of the clay.

units.leftText: Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
units.rightText: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, Neither shall my pressure be heavy upon thee.

units.leftText: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words:
units.rightText: Surely thou hast spoken in my hearing, And I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,

units.leftText: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me.
units.rightText: I am clean, without transgression; I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me:

units.leftText: Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.
units.rightText: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, He counteth me for his enemy;

units.leftText: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
units.rightText: He putteth my feet in the stocks, He marketh all my paths.

units.leftText: Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
units.rightText: Behold, I will answer thee, in this thou art not just; For God is greater than man.

units.leftText: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
units.rightText: Why dost thou strive against him, For that he giveth not account of any of his matters?
leftNotes: 33:13 Or that He answers for none of His actions

units.leftText: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
units.rightText: For God speaketh once, Yea twice, though man regardeth it not.

units.leftText: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds,
units.rightText: In a dream, in a vision of the night, When deep sleep falleth upon men, In slumberings upon the bed;

units.leftText: He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings
units.rightText: Then he openeth the ears of men, And sealeth their instruction,

units.leftText: to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride,
units.rightText: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, And hide pride from man;

units.leftText: to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.
units.rightText: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, And his life from perishing by the sword.

units.leftText: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones,
units.rightText: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, And with continual strife in his bones;

units.leftText: so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.
units.rightText: So that his life abhorreth bread, And his soul dainty food.

units.leftText: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude.
units.rightText: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; And his bones that were not seen stick out.

units.leftText: He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
units.rightText: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the pit, And his life to the destroyers.

units.leftText: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him,
units.rightText: If there be with him an angel, An interpreter, one among a thousand, To show unto man what is right for him;

units.leftText: to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’
units.rightText: Then God is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.

units.leftText: then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.
units.rightText: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s; He returneth to the days of his youth.

units.leftText: He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.
units.rightText: He prayeth unto God, and he is favorable unto him, So that he seeth his face with joy: And he restoreth unto man his righteousness.

units.leftText: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.
units.rightText: He singeth before men, and saith, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, And it profited me not:

units.leftText: He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’
units.rightText: He hath redeemed my soul from going into the pit, And my life shall behold the light.

units.leftText: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times,
units.rightText: Lo, all these things doth God work, Twice, yea thrice, with a man,

units.leftText: to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
units.rightText: To bring back his soul from the pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of the living.

units.leftText: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
units.rightText: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: Hold thy peace, and I will speak.

units.leftText: But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.
units.rightText: If thou hast anything to say, answer me: Speak, for I desire to justify thee.

units.leftText: But if not, then listen to me; be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.”
units.rightText: If not, hearken thou unto me: Hold thy peace, and I will teach thee wisdom.

units.leftText: Then Elihu continued:
units.rightText: Moreover Elihu answered and said,

units.leftText: “Hear my words, O wise men; give ear to me, O men of learning.
units.rightText: Hear my words, ye wise men; And give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

units.leftText: For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.
units.rightText: For the ear trieth words, As the palate tasteth food.

units.leftText: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
units.rightText: Let us choose for us that which is right: Let us know among ourselves what is good.

units.leftText: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
units.rightText: For Job hath said, I am righteous, And God hath taken away my right:

units.leftText: Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’
units.rightText: Notwithstanding my right I am accounted a liar; My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.

units.leftText: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?
units.rightText: What man is like Job, Who drinketh up scoffing like water,

units.leftText: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.
units.rightText: Who goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, And walketh with wicked men?

units.leftText: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
units.rightText: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing That he should delight himself with God.

units.leftText: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
units.rightText: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: Far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, And from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

units.leftText: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
units.rightText: For the work of a man will he render unto him, And cause every man to find according to his ways.

units.leftText: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
units.rightText: Yea, of a surety, God will not do wickedly, Neither will the Almighty pervert justice.

units.leftText: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
units.rightText: Who gave him a charge over the earth? Or who hath disposed the whole world?

units.leftText: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,
units.rightText: If he set his heart upon himself, If he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

units.leftText: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
units.rightText: All flesh shall perish together, And man shall turn again unto dust.

units.leftText: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
units.rightText: If now thou hast understanding, hear this: Hearken to the voice of my words.

units.leftText: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,
units.rightText: Shall even one that hateth justice govern? And wilt thou condemn him that is righteous and mighty?—

units.leftText: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
units.rightText: Him that saith to a king, Thou art vile, Or to nobles, Ye are wicked;

units.leftText: who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor? For they are all the work of His hands.
units.rightText: That respecteth not the persons of princes, Nor regardeth the rich more than the poor; For they all are the work of his hands.

units.leftText: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
units.rightText: In a moment they die, even at midnight; The people are shaken and pass away, And the mighty are taken away without hand.

units.leftText: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
units.rightText: For his eyes are upon the ways of a man, And he seeth all his goings.

units.leftText: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
units.rightText: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, Where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

units.leftText: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
units.rightText: For he needeth not further to consider a man, That he should go before God in judgment.

units.leftText: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
units.rightText: He breaketh in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, And setteth others in their stead.

units.leftText: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
units.rightText: Therefore he taketh knowledge of their works; And he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

units.leftText: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,
units.rightText: He striketh them as wicked men In the open sight of others;

units.leftText: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
units.rightText: Because they turned aside from following him, And would not have regard in any of his ways:

units.leftText: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
units.rightText: So that they caused the cry of the poor to come unto him, And he heard the cry of the afflicted.

units.leftText: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,
units.rightText: When he giveth quietness, who then can condemn? And when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? Alike whether it be done unto a nation, or unto a man:

units.leftText: that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people.
units.rightText: That the godless man reign not, That there be none to ensnare the people.

units.leftText: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
units.rightText: For hath any said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more:

units.leftText: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
units.rightText: That which I see not teach thou me: If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more?

units.leftText: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed Him? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
units.rightText: Shall his recompense be as thou wilt, that thou refusest it? For thou must choose, and not I: Therefore speak what thou knowest.

units.leftText: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:
units.rightText: Men of understanding will say unto me, Yea, every wise man that heareth me:

units.leftText: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
units.rightText: Job speaketh without knowledge, And his words are without wisdom.

units.leftText: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.
units.rightText: Would that Job were tried unto the end, Because of his answering like wicked men.

units.leftText: For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God.”
units.rightText: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin; He clappeth his hands among us, And multiplieth his words against God.

units.leftText: And Elihu went on to say:
units.rightText: Moreover Elihu answered and said,

units.leftText: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
units.rightText: Thinkest thou this to be thy right, Or sayest thou, My righteousness is more than God’s,

units.leftText: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
units.rightText: That thou sayest, What advantage will it be unto thee? And, What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?

units.leftText: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
units.rightText: I will answer thee, And thy companions with thee.

units.leftText: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
units.rightText: Look unto the heavens, and see; And behold the skies, which are higher than thou.

units.leftText: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
units.rightText: If thou hast sinned, what effectest thou against him? And if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

units.leftText: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
units.rightText: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? Or what receiveth he of thy hand?

units.leftText: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
units.rightText: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art; And thy righteousness may profit a son of man.

units.leftText: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
units.rightText: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

units.leftText: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
units.rightText: But none saith, Where is God my Maker, Who giveth songs in the night,

units.leftText: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
units.rightText: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, And maketh us wiser than the birds of the heavens?

units.leftText: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
units.rightText: There they cry, but none giveth answer, Because of the pride of evil men.

units.leftText: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
units.rightText: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, Neither will the Almighty regard it.

units.leftText: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,
units.rightText: How much less when thou sayest thou beholdest him not, The cause is before him, and thou waitest for him!

units.leftText: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!
units.rightText: But now, because he hath not visited in his anger, Neither doth he greatly regard arrogance;

units.leftText: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
units.rightText: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vanity; He multiplieth words without knowledge.

units.leftText: And Elihu continued:
units.rightText: Elihu also proceeded, and said,

units.leftText: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.
units.rightText: Suffer me a little, and I will show thee; For I have yet somewhat to say on God’s behalf.

units.leftText: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
units.rightText: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, And will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

units.leftText: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
units.rightText: For truly my words are not false: One that is perfect in knowledge is with thee.

units.leftText: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
units.rightText: Behold, God is mighty, and despiseth not any: He is mighty in strength of understanding.

units.leftText: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.
units.rightText: He preserveth not the life of the wicked, But giveth to the afflicted their right.

units.leftText: He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings and exalts them forever.
units.rightText: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: But with kings upon the throne He setteth them for ever, and they are exalted.

units.leftText: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,
units.rightText: And if they be bound in fetters, And be taken in the cords of affliction;

units.leftText: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.
units.rightText: Then he showeth them their work, And their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.

units.leftText: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.
units.rightText: He openeth also their ear to instruction, And commandeth that they return from iniquity.

units.leftText: If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity and their years in happiness.
units.rightText: If they hearken and serve him, They shall spend their days in prosperity, And their years in pleasures.

units.leftText: But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
units.rightText: But if they hearken not, they shall perish by the sword, And they shall die without knowledge.
leftNotes: 36:12 Or they will cross the river of death

units.leftText: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
units.rightText: But they that are godless in heart lay up anger: They cry not for help when he bindeth them.

units.leftText: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.
units.rightText: They die in youth, And their life perisheth among the unclean.

units.leftText: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.
units.rightText: He delivereth the afflicted by their affliction, And openeth their ear in oppression.

units.leftText: Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place, to a table full of richness.
units.rightText: Yea, he would have allured thee out of distress Into a broad place, where there is no straitness; And that which is set on thy table would be full of fatness.

units.leftText: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
units.rightText: But thou art full of the judgment of the wicked: Judgment and justice take hold on thee.

units.leftText: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.
units.rightText: For let not wrath stir thee up against chastisements; Neither let the greatness of the ransom turn thee aside.

units.leftText: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?
units.rightText: Will thy cry avail, that thou be not in distress, Or all the forces of thy strength?

units.leftText: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.
units.rightText: Desire not the night, When peoples are cut off in their place.

units.leftText: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.
units.rightText: Take heed, regard not iniquity: For this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

units.leftText: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
units.rightText: Behold, God doeth loftily in his power: Who is a teacher like unto him?

units.leftText: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?
units.rightText: Who hath enjoined him his way? Or who can say, Thou hast wrought unrighteousness?

units.leftText: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
units.rightText: Remember that thou magnify his work, Whereof men have sung.

units.leftText: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.
units.rightText: All men have looked thereon; Man beholdeth it afar off.

units.leftText: Indeed, God is great — beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.
units.rightText: Behold, God is great, and we know him not; The number of his years is unsearchable.

units.leftText: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,
units.rightText: For he draweth up the drops of water, Which distil in rain from his vapor,

units.leftText: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.
units.rightText: Which the skies pour down And drop upon man abundantly.

units.leftText: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?
units.rightText: Yea, can any understand the spreadings of the clouds, The thunderings of his pavilion?

units.leftText: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
units.rightText: Behold, he spreadeth his light around him; And he covereth the bottom of the sea.

units.leftText: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.
units.rightText: For by these he judgeth the peoples; He giveth food in abundance.

units.leftText: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
units.rightText: He covereth his hands with the lightning, And giveth it a charge that it strike the mark.

units.leftText: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.[’’]
units.rightText: The noise thereof telleth concerning him, The cattle also concerning the storm that cometh up.

units.leftText: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.
units.rightText: Yea, at this my heart trembleth, And is moved out of its place.

units.leftText: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
units.rightText: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, And the sound that goeth out of his mouth.

units.leftText: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: He sendeth it forth under the whole heaven, And his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
units.rightText: After it a voice roareth; He thundereth with the voice of his majesty; And he restraineth not the lightnings when his voice is heard.

units.leftText: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
units.rightText: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; Great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

units.leftText: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’
units.rightText: For he saith to the snow, Fall thou on the earth; Likewise to the shower of rain, And to the showers of his mighty rain.

units.leftText: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
units.rightText: He sealeth up the hand of every man, That all men whom he hath made may know it.

units.leftText: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.
units.rightText: Then the beasts go into coverts, And remain in their dens.

units.leftText: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
units.rightText: Out of the chamber of the south cometh the storm, And cold out of the north.

units.leftText: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.
units.rightText: By the breath of God ice is given; And the breadth of the waters is straitened.

units.leftText: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.
units.rightText: Yea, he ladeth the thick cloud with moisture; He spreadeth abroad the cloud of his lightning:

units.leftText: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.
units.rightText: And it is turned round about by his guidance, That they may do whatsoever he commandeth them Upon the face of the habitable world,

units.leftText: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.
units.rightText: Whether it be for correction, or for his land, Or for lovingkindness, that he cause it to come.

units.leftText: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
units.rightText: Hearken unto this, O Job: Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

units.leftText: Do you know how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash?
units.rightText: Dost thou know how God layeth his charge upon them, And causeth the lightning of his cloud to shine?

units.leftText: Do you understand how the clouds float, those wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
units.rightText: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, The wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

units.leftText: You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,
units.rightText: How thy garments are warm, When the earth is still by reason of the south wind?

units.leftText: can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?
units.rightText: Canst thou with him spread out the sky, Which is strong as a molten mirror?

units.leftText: Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.
units.rightText: Teach us what we shall say unto him; For we cannot set our speech in order by reason of darkness.

units.leftText: Should He be told that I want to speak? Would a man ask to be swallowed up ?
units.rightText: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
leftNotes: 37:20 Or speak without being swallowed up

units.leftText: Now no one can gaze at the sun when it is bright in the skies after the wind has swept them clean.
units.rightText: And now men see not the light which is bright in the skies; But the wind passeth, and cleareth them.

units.leftText: Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.
units.rightText: Out of the north cometh golden splendor: God hath upon him terrible majesty.

units.leftText: The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.
units.rightText: Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out: He is excellent in power; And in justice and plenteous righteousness he will not afflict.

units.leftText: Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.”
units.rightText: Men do therefore fear him: He regardeth not any that are wise of heart.

units.leftText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
units.rightText: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

units.leftText: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
units.rightText: Who is this that darkeneth counsel By words without knowledge?

units.leftText: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
units.rightText: Gird up now thy loins like a man; For I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

units.leftText: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
units.rightText: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if thou hast understanding.

units.leftText: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
units.rightText: Who determined the measures thereof, if thou knowest? Or who stretched the line upon it?

units.leftText: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
units.rightText: Whereupon were the foundations thereof fastened? Or who laid the corner-stone thereof,
leftNotes: 38:6 Or who set its core in place

units.leftText: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
units.rightText: When the morning stars sang together, And all the sons of God shouted for joy?

units.leftText: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
units.rightText: Or who shut up the sea with doors, When it brake forth, as if it had issued out of the womb;

units.leftText: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,
units.rightText: When I made clouds the garment thereof, And thick darkness a swaddling-band for it,

units.leftText: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,
units.rightText: And marked out for it my bound, And set bars and doors,

units.leftText: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
units.rightText: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further; And here shall thy proud waves be stayed?

units.leftText: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,
units.rightText: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days began, And caused the dayspring to know its place;

units.leftText: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
units.rightText: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked be shaken out of it?

units.leftText: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
units.rightText: It is changed as clay under the seal; And all things stand forth as a garment:

units.leftText: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
units.rightText: And from the wicked their light is withholden, And the high arm is broken.

units.leftText: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
units.rightText: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? Or hast thou walked in the recesses of the deep?

units.leftText: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
units.rightText: Have the gates of death been revealed unto thee? Or hast thou seen the gates of the shadow of death?

units.leftText: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
units.rightText: Hast thou comprehended the earth in its breadth? Declare, if thou knowest it all.

units.leftText: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,
units.rightText: Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And as for darkness, where is the place thereof,

units.leftText: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
units.rightText: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, And that thou shouldest discern the paths to the house thereof?

units.leftText: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
units.rightText: Doubtless, thou knowest, for thou wast then born, And the number of thy days is great!

units.leftText: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,
units.rightText: Hast thou entered the treasuries of the snow, Or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

units.leftText: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
units.rightText: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, Against the day of battle and war?

units.leftText: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
units.rightText: By what way is the light parted, Or the east wind scattered upon the earth?

units.leftText: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,
units.rightText: Who hath cleft a channel for the waterflood, Or the way for the lightning of the thunder;

units.leftText: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,
units.rightText: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; On the wilderness, wherein there is no man;

units.leftText: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
units.rightText: To satisfy the waste and desolate ground, And to cause the tender grass to spring forth?

units.leftText: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
units.rightText: Hath the rain a father? Or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

units.leftText: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,
units.rightText: Out of whose womb came the ice? And the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

units.leftText: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
units.rightText: The waters hide themselves and become like stone, And the face of the deep is frozen.

units.leftText: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
units.rightText: Canst thou bind the cluster of the Pleiades, Or loose the bands of Orion?

units.leftText: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
units.rightText: Canst thou lead forth the Mazzaroth in their season? Or canst thou guide the Bear with her train?
leftNotes: 38:32 Or bring forth Mazzaroth in its season

units.leftText: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
units.rightText: Knowest thou the ordinances of the heavens? Canst thou establish the dominion thereof in the earth?

units.leftText: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
units.rightText: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover thee?

units.leftText: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
units.rightText: Canst thou send forth lightnings, that they may go, And say unto thee, Here we are?

units.leftText: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
units.rightText: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who hath given understanding to the mind?
leftNotes: 38:36 Or Who has given the ibis wisdom, that is, wisdom about the flooding of the Nile

units.leftText: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens
units.rightText: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of heaven,

units.leftText: when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
units.rightText: When the dust runneth into a mass, And the clods cleave fast together?

units.leftText: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions
units.rightText: Canst thou hunt the prey for the lioness, Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

units.leftText: when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
units.rightText: When they couch in their dens, And abide in the covert to lie in wait?

units.leftText: Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God as they wander about for lack of food?[’’]
units.rightText: Who provideth for the raven his prey, When his young ones cry unto God, And wander for lack of food?

units.leftText: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
units.rightText: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? Or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

units.leftText: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
units.rightText: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? Or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

units.leftText: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
units.rightText: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, They cast out their pains.

units.leftText: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
units.rightText: Their young ones become strong, they grow up in the open field; They go forth, and return not again.

units.leftText: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
units.rightText: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? Or who hath loosed the bonds of the swift ass,

units.leftText: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
units.rightText: Whose home I have made the wilderness, And the salt land his dwelling-place?

units.leftText: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
units.rightText: He scorneth the tumult of the city, Neither heareth he the shoutings of the driver.

units.leftText: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
units.rightText: The range of the mountains is his pasture, And he searcheth after every green thing.

units.leftText: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
units.rightText: Will the wild-ox be content to serve thee? Or will he abide by thy crib?

units.leftText: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
units.rightText: Canst thou bind the wild-ox with his band in the furrow? Or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

units.leftText: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
units.rightText: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? Or wilt thou leave to him thy labor?

units.leftText: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
units.rightText: Wilt thou confide in him, that he will bring home thy seed, And gather the grain of thy threshing-floor?

units.leftText: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
units.rightText: The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; But are they the pinions and plumage of love?
leftNotes: 39:13 Pinions are the outer parts of a bird’s wings, including the flight feathers.

units.leftText: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
units.rightText: For she leaveth her eggs on the earth, And warmeth them in the dust,

units.leftText: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
units.rightText: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, Or that the wild beast may trample them.

units.leftText: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
units.rightText: She dealeth hardly with her young ones, as if they were not hers: Though her labor be in vain, she is without fear;

units.leftText: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
units.rightText: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, Neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

units.leftText: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
units.rightText: What time she lifteth up herself on high, She scorneth the horse and his rider.

units.leftText: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
units.rightText: Hast thou given the horse his might? Hast thou clothed his neck with the quivering mane?

units.leftText: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
units.rightText: Hast thou made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is terrible.

units.leftText: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
units.rightText: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: He goeth out to meet the armed men.

units.leftText: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
units.rightText: He mocketh at fear, and is not dismayed; Neither turneth he back from the sword.

units.leftText: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
units.rightText: The quiver rattleth against him, The flashing spear and the javelin.

units.leftText: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
units.rightText: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage; Neither believeth he that it is the voice of the trumpet.

units.leftText: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar, the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
units.rightText: As oft as the trumpet soundeth he saith, Aha! And he smelleth the battle afar off, The thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

units.leftText: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
units.rightText: Is it by thy wisdom that the hawk soareth, And stretcheth her wings toward the south?

units.leftText: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
units.rightText: Is it at thy command that the eagle mounteth up, And maketh her nest on high?

units.leftText: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
units.rightText: On the cliff she dwelleth, and maketh her home, Upon the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

units.leftText: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
units.rightText: From thence she spieth out the prey; Her eyes behold it afar off.

units.leftText: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
units.rightText: Her young ones also suck up blood: And where the slain are, there is she.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Job:
units.rightText: Moreover Jehovah answered Job, and said,

units.leftText: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
units.rightText: Shall he that cavilleth contend with the Almighty? He that argueth with God, let him answer it.

units.leftText: Then Job answered the LORD:
units.rightText: Then Job answered Jehovah, and said,

units.leftText: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
units.rightText: Behold, I am of small account; what shall I answer thee? I lay my hand upon my mouth.

units.leftText: I have spoken once, but I have no answer — twice, but I have nothing to add.” The LORD Challenges Job Again
units.rightText: Once have I spoken, and I will not answer; Yea, twice, but I will proceed no further.

units.leftText: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
units.rightText: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

units.leftText: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
units.rightText: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

units.leftText: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
units.rightText: Wilt thou even annul my judgment? Wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be justified?

units.leftText: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
units.rightText: Or hast thou an arm like God? And canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

units.leftText: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
units.rightText: Deck thyself now with excellency and dignity; And array thyself with honor and majesty.

units.leftText: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
units.rightText: Pour forth the overflowings of thine anger; And look upon every one that is proud, and abase him.

units.leftText: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
units.rightText: Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; And tread down the wicked where they stand.

units.leftText: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
units.rightText: Hide them in the dust together; Bind their faces in the hidden place.

units.leftText: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
units.rightText: Then will I also confess of thee That thine own right hand can save thee.

units.leftText: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
units.rightText: Behold now, behemoth, which I made as well as thee; He eateth grass as an ox.

units.leftText: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
units.rightText: Lo now, his strength is in his loins, And his force is in the muscles of his belly.

units.leftText: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
units.rightText: He moveth his tail like a cedar: The sinews of his thighs are knit together.

units.leftText: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
units.rightText: His bones are as tubes of brass; His limbs are like bars of iron.

units.leftText: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
units.rightText: He is the chief of the ways of God: He only that made him giveth him his sword.

units.leftText: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
units.rightText: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, Where all the beasts of the field do play.

units.leftText: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
units.rightText: He lieth under the lotus-trees, In the covert of the reed, and the fen.
leftNotes: 40:21 Or bramble bushes; also in verse 22

units.leftText: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
units.rightText: The lotus-trees cover him with their shade; The willows of the brook compass him about.

units.leftText: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
units.rightText: Behold, if a river overflow, he trembleth not; He is confident, though a Jordan swell even to his mouth.

units.leftText: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?[’’]
units.rightText: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, Or pierce through his nose with a snare?

units.leftText: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
units.rightText: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a fishhook? Or press down his tongue with a cord?

units.leftText: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
units.rightText: Canst thou put a rope into his nose? Or pierce his jaw through with a hook?

units.leftText: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
units.rightText: Will he make many supplications unto thee? Or will he speak soft words unto thee?

units.leftText: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
units.rightText: Will he make a covenant with thee, That thou shouldest take him for a servant for ever?

units.leftText: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
units.rightText: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? Or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

units.leftText: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
units.rightText: Will the bands of fishermen make traffic of him? Will they part him among the merchants?

units.leftText: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
units.rightText: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons, Or his head with fish-spears?

units.leftText: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
units.rightText: Lay thy hand upon him; Remember the battle, and do so no more.

units.leftText: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
units.rightText: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: Will not one be cast down even at the sight of him?

units.leftText: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
units.rightText: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up; Who then is he that can stand before me?

units.leftText: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
units.rightText: Who hath first given unto me, that I should repay him? Whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

units.leftText: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
units.rightText: I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, Nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.

units.leftText: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
units.rightText: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?
leftNotes: 41:13 Or Who can come within his double mail?

units.leftText: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
units.rightText: Who can open the doors of his face? Round about his teeth is terror.

units.leftText: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
units.rightText: His strong scales are his pride, Shut up together as with a close seal.

units.leftText: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
units.rightText: One is so near to another, That no air can come between them.

units.leftText: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
units.rightText: They are joined one to another; They stick together, so that they cannot be sundered.

units.leftText: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
units.rightText: His sneezings flash forth light, And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

units.leftText: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
units.rightText: Out of his mouth go burning torches, And sparks of fire leap forth.

units.leftText: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
units.rightText: Out of his nostrils a smoke goeth, As of a boiling pot and burning rushes.

units.leftText: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
units.rightText: His breath kindleth coals, And a flame goeth forth from his mouth.

units.leftText: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
units.rightText: In his neck abideth strength, And terror danceth before him.

units.leftText: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
units.rightText: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: They are firm upon him; they cannot be moved.

units.leftText: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
units.rightText: His heart is as firm as a stone; Yea, firm as the nether millstone.

units.leftText: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
units.rightText: When he raiseth himself up, the mighty are afraid: By reason of consternation they are beside themselves.

units.leftText: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
units.rightText: If one lay at him with the sword, it cannot avail; Nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

units.leftText: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
units.rightText: He counteth iron as straw, And brass as rotten wood.

units.leftText: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
units.rightText: The arrow cannot make him flee: Sling-stones are turned with him into stubble.

units.leftText: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
units.rightText: Clubs are counted as stubble: He laugheth at the rushing of the javelin.

units.leftText: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
units.rightText: His underparts are like sharp potsherds: He spreadeth as it were a threshing-wain upon the mire.

units.leftText: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
units.rightText: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: He maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

units.leftText: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
units.rightText: He maketh a path to shine after him; One would think the deep to be hoary.

units.leftText: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
units.rightText: Upon earth there is not his like, That is made without fear.

units.leftText: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
units.rightText: He beholdeth everything that is high: He is king over all the sons of pride.

units.leftText: Then Job replied to the LORD:
units.rightText: Then Job answered Jehovah, and said,

units.leftText: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
units.rightText: I know that thou canst do all things, And that no purpose of thine can be restrained.

units.leftText: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
units.rightText: Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore have I uttered that which I understood not, Things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

units.leftText: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
units.rightText: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak; I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

units.leftText: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
units.rightText: I had heard of thee by the hearing of the ear; But now mine eye seeth thee:

units.leftText: Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.” The LORD Rebukes Job’s Friends
units.rightText: Wherefore I abhor myself, And repent in dust and ashes.

units.leftText: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, after Jehovah had spoken these words unto Job, Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends; for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

units.leftText: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
units.rightText: Now therefore, take unto you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt-offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you; for him will I accept, that I deal not with you after your folly; for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

units.leftText: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer. The LORD Blesses Job
units.rightText: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as Jehovah commanded them: and Jehovah accepted Job.

units.leftText: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
units.rightText: And Jehovah turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: and Jehovah gave Job twice as much as he had before.

units.leftText: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
units.rightText: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him concerning all the evil that Jehovah had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one a ring of gold.
leftNotes: 42:11 Hebrew a kesitah; the value or weight of the kesitah is no longer known.

units.leftText: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
units.rightText: So Jehovah blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: and he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses.

units.leftText: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
units.rightText: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

units.leftText: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
units.rightText: And he called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.

units.leftText: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
units.rightText: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

units.leftText: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
units.rightText: And after this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations.

units.leftText: And so Job died, old and full of years.
units.rightText: So Job died, being old and full of days.
